20aqR8E6En.one_liner: Activation steering that removes the memory-induced, execution-ward shift in representations to restore agent safety after experience-driven evolution.
20aqR8E6En.problem: Evolved experience memory degrades agent safety, and existing mitigations modify the evolution mechanism, the prompt, or add agent components instead of correcting the model itself.
20aqR8E6En.method: Uses the memory-free forward pass of the same request as a per-request reference and selectively removes the execution-ward component of the memory-induced representation shift, with no change to model weights, prompt, evolved memory, or evolution algorithm.
20aqR8E6En.key_idea: Retrieved experience shifts harmful-request representations toward execution along a safety-relevant direction; subtract that component, measured against the memory-free forward pass.
20aqR8E6En.evidence: Experiments (settings not given in the abstract) show the method mitigates memory-induced safety degradation while largely preserving benign performance.

xowZZM2XqB.one_liner: Differential scaling law allocating diffusion language model capacity and data by timestep, realized with quantile stratified sampling and sparse MoE.
xowZZM2XqB.problem: Chinchilla-style compute-optimal recipes allocate capacity and data uniformly across the diffusion process, though DLM loss varies substantially with diffusion timestep, leaving compute underutilized.
xowZZM2XqB.method: Ermine characterizes instantaneous loss through time-dependent capacity and data densities, derives the optimal allocation under a fixed compute budget, and realizes it with quantile-based stratified sampling over timesteps and a sparse Mixture-of-Experts architecture.
xowZZM2XqB.key_idea: Model loss at each diffusion timestep with time-dependent capacity and data densities and solve for the compute-optimal allocation over time.
xowZZM2XqB.evidence: OpenWebText validation perplexity and five zero-shot commonsense reasoning benchmarks, compared with dense DLMs, Chinchilla-optimal training, and autoregressive models.
xowZZM2XqB.claimed_gains: Accelerates Chinchilla-optimal training by 1.35x, improves compute efficiency over dense DLMs by 1.84x, narrows the DLM-ARM compute-optimal gap from 17.56x to 9.57x, and reaches validation perplexity 17.63 on OpenWebText, outperforming existing ARMs and DLMs at 1.1x10^21 FLOPs with only 30-50% of their training FLOPs.

3WJt45k8b3.one_liner: Aligns spectral modalities with orthogonal rotations and learns cross-view features at a selected encoder block for any-scenario person re-identification.
3WJt45k8b3.problem: Existing any-scenario ReID methods handle spectral and aerial-ground view variations through joint scenario alignment without accounting for their distinct characteristics.
3WJt45k8b3.method: OCSFA combines orthogonal rotations with mean alignment to map spectral modalities into a shared reference frame, learned by making modality-view prototypes agree with an identity consensus prototype. LLCVL compares within-view and cross-view similarities across encoder blocks to locate a supervision boundary, then applies bidirectional cross-view contrastive learning at that block.
3WJt45k8b3.key_idea: Handle spectral gaps with distance-preserving orthogonal alignment to a shared frame, and view gaps with contrastive supervision at an encoder block chosen by cross-view similarity statistics.
3WJt45k8b3.evidence: Experiments on the WHU-MARS benchmark across different evaluation protocols (abstract cut off).
3WJt45k8b3.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract is cut off before its numbers.

HDZmeQWsiP.one_liner: Training-free perceptual distance from a frozen vision encoder's Jacobian, using E[J^T J] as a fixed metric tensor on early features.
HDZmeQWsiP.problem: Pixel error ignores human vision, while the most accurate perceptual distances are fitted to human judgments, tying them to fixed data and resolution.
HDZmeQWsiP.method: JLD uses the encoder Jacobian to find directions in early feature space that most affect the encoder output, forming the fixed metric tensor E[J^T J] (the Jacobian lens), which is fitted once from unlabeled images and defines a pullback metric in pixel space.
HDZmeQWsiP.key_idea: Weight early patch-feature differences by the expected Jacobian metric E[J^T J] of a frozen encoder, combining the locality of early features with the output sensitivity of later layers.
HDZmeQWsiP.evidence: Four standard perceptual databases (including TID2013) against LPIPS, DISTS, PieAPP and DreamSim, plus resolution-robustness tests.
HDZmeQWsiP.claimed_gains: JLD outperforms LPIPS, DISTS, PieAPP and DreamSim on four perceptual databases and is robust to resolution changes (for contrast, DISTS correlation on TID2013 falls from 0.815 to 0.717 when resolution doubles), with the lens fitted from 100 unlabeled images in about 35 seconds.

2TDpev8lZE.one_liner: DPR recalibrates token-level hidden states in forecasting backbones through local-context perception and soft routing over a response basis.
2TDpev8lZE.problem: Local temporal patterns shift across regimes, and forecasting backbones lack an explicit way to separate shared representation learning from local feature-gain adaptation.
2TDpev8lZE.method: A Perceive-Route-Modulate pipeline computes a soft-routing distribution over a compact learned response basis to produce a context-dependent modulation vector that recalibrates hidden states by a residual Hadamard product, and DPRNet is a minimal standalone version.
2TDpev8lZE.key_idea: A soft-routing mixture over a compact learned basis yields a per-token modulation vector applied to hidden states by residual Hadamard product, separating gain adaptation from shared representation.
2TDpev8lZE.evidence: Ten forecasting backbones across 95 backbone-dataset pairs, and DPRNet on 11 benchmarks with low measured computational cost.
2TDpev8lZE.claimed_gains: DPR matches or improves the raw backbone's MSE in 87 of 95 backbone-dataset pairs (91.6%), with larger gains where local volatility variation is greater.

rJ5oUy2nuv.one_liner: N-GDOI learns the interaction graph of restless bandits online using Fisher-weighted exploration and optimistic stochastic rollout planning.
rJ5oUy2nuv.problem: In restless bandits where interventions spread over an unknown sparse graph with delayed, persistent, nonlinear effects, reward-seeking actions may not reveal the graph, especially when responses saturate.
rJ5oUy2nuv.method: Combines derivative-weighted Fisher exploration and localized sparse nonlinear graph estimation with optimistic stochastic rollout planning over graph confidence sets, accounting for model uncertainty and nonlinear trajectory noise.
rJ5oUy2nuv.key_idea: Exploration is weighted by the derivative of the nonlinear response to probe informative Fisher directions, and planning is optimistic over the graph confidence set.
rJ5oUy2nuv.evidence: High-probability graph-recovery guarantees under adaptively collected data, stability of stochastic rollout values under graph perturbations, regret bounds, and experiments (the abstract is cut off).
rJ5oUy2nuv.claimed_gains: Truncated rollout regret of O~(T^{2/3}) under scheduled Fisher-informative exploration, improving to O~(sqrt(T)) when reward-seeking actions give persistent Fisher excitation.

Ebl1OftZNY.one_liner: Early token pruning for visual place recognition that predicts late-layer attention token rankings from early representations.
Ebl1OftZNY.problem: Aggressive early token pruning in VPR transformers degrades performance, while the reliable oracle ranking from final-block attention needs an extra forward pass.
Ebl1OftZNY.method: OraP anticipates late-emerging token rankings from early representations, preserving only selection-relevant ranking relationships rather than exact attention values, so pruning happens in a single forward pass and applies to various transformer-based VPR models.
Ebl1OftZNY.key_idea: Predict the final-block attention token ranking from early features by preserving only ranking relationships, not attention values or distributions.
Ebl1OftZNY.evidence: An oracle study showing final-block attention rankings guide near-lossless early pruning, and experiments on representative transformer-based VPR models against existing token reduction methods under the same early pruning setting.
Ebl1OftZNY.claimed_gains: Substantially outperforms existing token reduction methods under the same early pruning setting; the abstract's specific results for removing 50% of the patch tokens are cut off in the input.

ld4BYzroVP.one_liner: Context runtime for long-horizon agents that carries forward reusable task objects with evidence-bound updates instead of replaying interaction history.
ld4BYzroVP.problem: Long-horizon agents repeatedly reprocess interaction histories describing how progress was made, rather than organizing context around the reusable progress itself.
ld4BYzroVP.method: CarryOn builds a context view from continuation carriers, complementary execution context and a live tail of recent interactions. It maintains carrier records across folds, revising affected records against bound evidence and environment checks while carrying forward unaffected ones.
ld4BYzroVP.key_idea: Incrementally update per-object carrier records at each context fold, revising only records affected by new evidence, instead of reconstructing the full representation.
ld4BYzroVP.claimed_gains: Gains of 5.8% and 7.0% on OSWorld2.0 and BrowseComp-Plus while reducing total token usage by 51.9% and 22.9%, respectively.

45wFFQOeSK.one_liner: Data-free neural skinning fields for real-time cutting simulation, using a cut-dependent lifting coordinate and physics-informed self-supervision.
45wFFQOeSK.problem: Cutting deformable objects creates displacement discontinuities that are hard to handle in reduced-order simulation.
45wFFQOeSK.method: Neural skinning represents full-space deformation in a compact subspace, and a geometry-derived lifting-and-restriction formulation adds a cut-dependent scalar coordinate that separates the two sides of a cut and vanishes at its boundary. Skinning fields are learned by minimizing expected potential energy with cut-aware Monte Carlo importance sampling, a cross-side jump constraint and an orthogonality term.
45wFFQOeSK.key_idea: Augment coordinates with a cut-dependent lifting coordinate so neural skinning weights can jump across the cut yet stay continuous at its boundary, trained by energy minimization.
45wFFQOeSK.evidence: Real-time reduced-order cut simulation shown across diverse 3D objects and cut configurations, on meshes and Gaussian splats, and in robot interaction simulation.

l4MAf7JUTf.one_liner: Calibrates finite policy covers in zero-sum Block games by linear programming over decoder-event coverage constraints, without identifying the latent decoder.
l4MAf7JUTf.problem: A policy cover can reach every important state while its uniform mixture gives poor data for equilibrium learning.
l4MAf7JUTf.method: Under common emissions and a finite decoder class containing the true decoder, constraints on all candidate-decoder events are equivalent at the population level to latent coverage constraints. The constraints are estimated from shared rollouts and implemented by linear programming, with a polynomial-time implementation for a hidden-coordinate class.
l4MAf7JUTf.key_idea: Impose coverage constraints on events of every candidate decoder, which at population level equal latent-state coverage constraints, and solve for the policy mixture by linear program.
l4MAf7JUTf.evidence: Theoretical sample-complexity guarantees under finite-class fitting conditions, an adaptive lower bound in a three-stage family, and fixed-budget experiments.
l4MAf7JUTf.claimed_gains: The Nash guarantee replaces the library size M by a coverage factor R at most min{M,S} in the fitting budget, and in a three-stage family O~(M+eps^-2) episodes match an adaptive lower bound up to logarithms while uniform sampling needs Omega(M eps^-2).

FlnhnuM3qO.one_liner: On-policy self-distillation post-trains few-step autoregressive video generators using a teacher whose history is replaced by real-video context.
FlnhnuM3qO.problem: Few-step autoregressive video generators distilled from short-clip teachers suffer error accumulation and weakened motion dynamics during long rollouts.
FlnhnuM3qO.method: Student and teacher are both the DMD-distilled few-step model: the student rolls out on its own KV cache while the teacher is evaluated at the same denoising states with older history replaced by real-video context. Both share an initial real-video prefix and the teacher keeps its most recent model-generated chunk.
FlnhnuM3qO.key_idea: Supervise the student on its own rollout states with a teacher that conditions on a cleaner cache where older history is replaced by real-video context.
FlnhnuM3qO.evidence: Experiments on Self-Forcing and LongLive report improved visual quality and motion; further details are cut off in the abstract.

n8NBtWMYf2.one_liner: Causal patching reveals a four-part VLM mechanism for listing objects: binding heads, a cursor, selection, and gaze heads.
n8NBtWMYf2.problem: It is unclear how a VLM that names one object at a time, rarely repeating itself, decides where to look next.
n8NBtWMYf2.method: Binding heads resolve text tokens into pointers to image regions and bind each written answer to its region, producing a cursor of progress; a select step picks the nearest unwritten region after the cursor or stops; gaze heads execute the pointer and return a concept that language heads and late MLPs turn into a word. Each part is validated by causal patching.
n8NBtWMYf2.key_idea: A cursor tracks how far into the image the answer list has progressed, and a select step points to the nearest unwritten region.
n8NBtWMYf2.evidence: Causal patching in Qwen3-VL models on a synthetic visual retrieval task, tests against alternative hypotheses, and checks across input formats, natural photographs, languages, and model sizes from 2B to 32B.

arRWIJAbQ0.one_liner: Multimodal JEPA foundation model for molecules that predicts masked biochemical modalities in latent space.
arRWIJAbQ0.problem: Molecular foundation models suffer from chemically invalid augmentations, modality collapse, and incomplete representation of biochemical environments.
arRWIJAbQ0.method: Mol-JEPA uses modality masking, rather than molecular perturbations, to exploit molecular structures, cellular phenotypes, binding affinities, ADMET profiles, quantum chemistry simulations, and other drug discovery data. It learns by predicting the masked modalities in latent space.
arRWIJAbQ0.key_idea: Mask whole biochemical modalities and predict them in latent space (JEPA) instead of perturbing molecules, avoiding chemically invalid augmentations.
arRWIJAbQ0.evidence: Evaluated across various drug discovery benchmarks (specific benchmarks are not named in the abstract).
arRWIJAbQ0.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says only 'strong performance').

Uilsbq8dfC.one_liner: LumaFlux adapts a frozen diffusion transformer with rectified-flow transport and a monotone spline tone decoder for SDR-to-HDR conversion.
Uilsbq8dfC.problem: Existing inverse tone mapping relies on fixed tone mappings or narrow training degradations, causing clipped highlights, chromatic shifts and temporally unstable tone reproduction.
Uilsbq8dfC.method: A DiT conditioned on physical measurements of the SDR input is adapted by training 0.57% of parameters, combining Physically-Guided Adaptation, Perceptual Cross-Modulation, an HDR Residual Coupler and a Rational-Quadratic Spline tone-field decoder; HDR latents come from rectified-flow transport in 8 steps, and video uses shared bridge noise and temporally smoothed spline parameters.
Uilsbq8dfC.key_idea: Decode HDR with a monotone rational-quadratic spline tone field, which preserves input luminance ordering, on top of a parameter-efficiently adapted DiT with direct rectified-flow transport.
Uilsbq8dfC.evidence: Training on a curated 314,396-pair UGC and PGC corpus in PQ BT.2020 and evaluation on LumaEval, a protocol spanning eight SDR degradation types, with video handled without temporal modules.
Uilsbq8dfC.claimed_gains: Trains only 0.57% of total parameters and reconstructs HDR latents in 8 steps; the TLDR says it leads all seven LumaEval metrics, but the abstract is truncated before the results.

U8RXjd4kKa.one_liner: RePT post-trains traffic agents only on lowest-scoring scenes, adding a trajectory-cluster diversity bonus to keep alternative behaviors sampled.
U8RXjd4kKa.problem: RL post-training for traffic simulation rewards resemblance to logs across the whole training set, so most gradient goes to already-solved scenes while on hard scenes all rollouts fail with near-equal rewards and the update reinforces the least bad failure.
U8RXjd4kKa.method: RePT selects, once before training, the scenes the supervised model scores lowest and post-trains only on them. It clusters rollouts by joint trajectories, rewards each rollout for standing outside the others' clusters, and withholds the bonus once its realism falls a margin below the group mean.
U8RXjd4kKa.key_idea: Concentrate post-training on the supervised model's worst scenes and reward rollouts for being outside other rollouts' trajectory clusters, gated by a realism margin.
U8RXjd4kKa.evidence: The abstract describes post-training on multi-agent traffic scenes such as merges and unprotected turns; datasets and results are cut off.

qd37WgGvOq.one_liner: MTEdit builds multi-turn image editing data by generating several editing states jointly on one packed canvas to reduce quality drift.
qd37WgGvOq.problem: Constructing high-quality multi-turn image editing training data is hard because sequential rollout accumulates errors and introduces visual-quality drift across turns.
qd37WgGvOq.method: A pipeline centered on packed trajectory canvas (PTC) generation jointly generates multiple editing states in one visual context, yielding the MTEdit dataset of 500K trajectories (up to 8 turns, average 5.38) for step-wise and context-aware editing. The authors add MTEdit-Bench and fine-tune Qwen-Image-Edit-Causal into Qwen-Image-MTEdit.
qd37WgGvOq.key_idea: Generate multiple editing states jointly within one canvas rather than by sequential rollout, so errors and quality drift do not compound across turns.
qd37WgGvOq.evidence: Fine-tuning Qwen-Image-Edit-Causal on MTEdit and evaluating closed- and open-source editing models on MTEdit-Bench for instruction following, content consistency, drift resistance, and history use.
qd37WgGvOq.claimed_gains: The dataset has 500K trajectories with up to 8 turns and an average of 5.38 turns, and the TLDR says the fine-tuned model is the strongest open-source model evaluated on MTEdit-Bench; no scores are stated.

i7Qt8F1GO0.one_liner: Unmerge treats unlearning as subtracting a low-rank forget component, fit in forget activation subspaces, from the merged task vector.
i7Qt8F1GO0.problem: Gradient-based approximate unlearning needs data-dependent hyperparameter search, struggles when forget and retain knowledge are entangled, and gives little insight into where unlearning happens in the network.
i7Qt8F1GO0.method: Unmerge casts unlearning as the inverse of finetuning: subtracting a learned forget component from the merged task vector to recover the retain task vector. It factorizes the forget component as B Q_F^T over a low-rank forget-activation subspace and optimizes three goals: match the merged vector inside the forget span, suppress leakage into the retain span, and bound the correction size.
i7Qt8F1GO0.key_idea: Subtract a low-rank forget task vector, built on the few dominant directions of forget activations per layer, while bounding leakage into the retain span.
i7Qt8F1GO0.evidence: Lemma 3.2 bounds the low-rank approximation residual by the tail eigenvalues of the forget-activation covariance, and the abstract states the three objectives provably bound forget leakage; empirical results are cut off.

Oqm561GvVP.one_liner: ESCD supervises the total student probability of byte-compatible completions of teacher tokens for cross-tokenizer on-policy distillation.
Oqm561GvVP.problem: With different tokenizers, a teacher token may need several student tokens, and once the student has produced a prefix the teacher specifies the required completion but not how probability splits among valid continuations.
Oqm561GvVP.method: Event-Set Completion Distillation aggregates prefix-related teacher events and supervises the total probability of byte-compatible one-step student completions, complementing cross-tokenizer probability alignment. It reuses student trajectories and predictions, with no extra rollouts and no change to the student vocabulary.
Oqm561GvVP.key_idea: Supervise the summed probability over all one-step student tokens that complete the teacher's remaining bytes, instead of dictating how it divides among them.
Oqm561GvVP.evidence: Experiments on mathematics, code, and scientific reasoning across model families and tokenizers, extending to MoE distillation from a 1T teacher.
Oqm561GvVP.claimed_gains: Consistent gains in mathematics, code, and scientific reasoning across model families and tokenizers; no numbers are visible in the truncated abstract.

YTjV3kptiD.one_liner: Fine-tuned video DiT placing egocentric and up to three exocentric views on one canvas, with task-specific conditioning masks.
YTjV3kptiD.problem: Most cross-view generators translate between egocentric and exocentric video in one predetermined direction, so different directions and temporal completions need separate models.
YTjV3kptiD.method: EgoU fine-tunes a pretrained video DiT on a shared canvas holding one egocentric and up to three exocentric views, expressing tasks through conditioning masks and optional text prompts. It adds view-type embeddings, a cross-attention branch for scene geometry and the wearer's head trajectory, and an auxiliary pose loss for exocentric human motion.
YTjV3kptiD.key_idea: Express diverse ego-exo generation tasks as conditioning masks over one shared multi-view video canvas, so a single set of parameters handles all directions and temporal completions.
YTjV3kptiD.evidence: Trained on EgoExoVideo-600K (604,113 synchronized ego-exo clip pairs) and evaluated on EgoU-Benchmark, which scores all tasks.

eHpgsTtmzX.one_liner: Adds relational abstractions from unsupervised object-centric representations to diffusion models to solve spatial reasoning puzzles.
eHpgsTtmzX.problem: Diffusion models approximate pixel-space distributions without learning the logical rules behind puzzles defined by visible clues and consistent solutions.
eHpgsTtmzX.method: The framework uses unsupervised object discovery and abstractions of object relations as structural primitives that guide the generative representation space during training and inference. The authors also introduce a generative spatial reasoning benchmark with four puzzle datasets.
eHpgsTtmzX.key_idea: Condition diffusion on relational abstractions computed from discovered objects so generation is guided by structural primitives rather than pixel statistics alone.
eHpgsTtmzX.evidence: A new benchmark of four human-solvable-puzzle-inspired datasets, with out-of-distribution generalization tests.
eHpgsTtmzX.claimed_gains: Relational abstractions significantly improve diffusion models' reasoning on complex tasks and generalize robustly out of distribution; no numbers stated.

PQbjqMbY3d.one_liner: Lightweight module letting each document page's visual tokens attend to neighbor pages via masked attention with directional gates.
PQbjqMbY3d.problem: Multi-page document vision-language models encode pages independently, so visual tokens lack adjacent-page content and the language model reasons over representations formed in isolation.
PQbjqMbY3d.method: DocSEAM sits between a pretrained vision encoder and the language model; for each page it forms a local triplet with its two neighbors, applies center-anchored masked self-attention with directional salience gates, and returns only the enriched center-page tokens so the token count is unchanged. Training uses a supervised cross-page warm-up and multi-page fine-tuning with DocSEAM frozen.
PQbjqMbY3d.key_idea: Center-anchored masked self-attention over a page and its two neighbors, with directional salience gates, injects local cross-page context while returning only center-page tokens.
PQbjqMbY3d.evidence: Five multi-page document VQA benchmarks with a 9B-parameter model, plus controlled re-pagination experiments measuring boundary sensitivity and cross-page span localization.
PQbjqMbY3d.claimed_gains: The 9B-parameter model is reported to achieve the best results among open-weight models on five multi-page document VQA benchmarks, with reduced sensitivity to boundary placement under re-pagination and no scores given.

zfQ3A1YLCN.one_liner: Multi-agent long-video system where an Orchestrator spawns parallel interval Executors that return findings plus supporting visuals.
zfQ3A1YLCN.problem: Agentic long-video systems inspect intervals sequentially, reprocess interaction history, and summarize local observations in text, which hides fine-grained visual detail from the global reasoner.
zfQ3A1YLCN.method: Videopus has an Orchestrator coordinating interval-specific Executors. Parallel Task Spawn batches inspections from the same evidence state, and Multimodal Evidence Aggregation returns structured findings with a compact set of supporting visuals, alternating parallel inspection with evidence-guided refinement.
zfQ3A1YLCN.key_idea: Run interval inspections in parallel and return structured findings with selected visuals so the global reasoner works on a compact, visually checkable evidence state.
zfQ3A1YLCN.evidence: Six video benchmarks, compared with prior methods on accuracy, token use, sequential rounds and persistent-context reuse.
zfQ3A1YLCN.claimed_gains: Outperforms the best prior methods across six video benchmarks while reducing token use and sequential rounds; no numbers stated.

vW2hr4Awpk.one_liner: Adaptively routes reward-driven updates across cross-modal layers and reweights multiple rewards during forward-process RL for joint audio-video diffusion.
vW2hr4Awpk.problem: Multi-reward RL for joint audio-video diffusion uses fixed update routing and reward weights, which cannot track how the model's functions and reward conflicts evolve during training.
vW2hr4Awpk.method: Cross-Modal Influence-Guided Routing uses bidirectional cross-attention responses to reweight token-aware losses and scale gradients across cross-modal layers. Preference-Preserving Modality-Aware Reweighting keeps predefined weights as priors and adds branch-specific reward-gradient interactions as residual corrections after warm-up.
vW2hr4Awpk.key_idea: Use cross-attention responses as a proxy for cross-modal influence to localize updates, and correct fixed reward weights with reward-gradient interactions after warm-up.
vW2hr4Awpk.evidence: Applied to DiffusionNFT forward-process RL for joint audio-video diffusion; the visible abstract is cut off before experiments.

QEc019wr7t.one_liner: Adapts an object-centric 3D generator to single-image indoor and outdoor scene meshes with distance-adaptive chunks and 2D-3D lifting.
QEc019wr7t.problem: Pretrained 3D object generators work on isolated objects in a fixed canonical volume and outdoor 3D scene data is limited, so single-image scene generation across indoor and outdoor scenes is hard.
QEc019wr7t.method: The method redesigns an object-centric generator (e.g., Trellis 2) by partitioning the scene into chunks that scale with camera distance and lifting image features for explicit 2D-3D correspondence and awareness of free space, observed surface and unobserved region. It also synthesizes about 4,000 outdoor scenes for training.
QEc019wr7t.key_idea: Partition scenes into chunks sized by distance from the camera and condition the generator on lifted image features that mark free, observed and unobserved space.
QEc019wr7t.evidence: Tanks and Temples, ScanNet++ and in-the-wild images.
QEc019wr7t.claimed_gains: Outperforms all baselines in geometric accuracy and perceptual quality on indoor and outdoor scenes; no numbers stated.

fCPdxfZtDn.one_liner: Adversarial attacks on world-action models that use small visual perturbations to desynchronize imagined futures from executed actions.
fCPdxfZtDn.problem: World-action models are assumed robust or safe because actions can be checked against imagined futures, but the authors argue this assumption is fragile.
fCPdxfZtDn.method: BadWAM defines World-Action Drift Attacks along two criteria, attack strength and stealthiness: an action-only attack that drives task-failing actions, and an imagination-preserving attack that induces harmful action shifts while keeping the predicted future close to its clean imagination.
fCPdxfZtDn.key_idea: Perturb visual inputs to push actions toward failure while constraining the predicted future to stay close to its clean imagination, breaking the imagination-action link.
fCPdxfZtDn.evidence: The abstract is truncated before experiments; no models, benchmarks, or results are visible.

Fgbe7fEJsv.one_liner: Decision-conditioned routing that selects which encoded data sources a frozen VLA policy uses at each step, via learned utility estimates.
Fgbe7fEJsv.problem: VLA policies use heterogeneous observations, but the relevance of each data source changes during task execution.
Fgbe7fEJsv.method: DataRouter maps native source representations and intermediate VLA states into a shared space to estimate context-dependent source utilities; one utility estimator supports fixed-budget, threshold, adaptive-budget, and cost-aware inference rules. Only lightweight routing components are trained from demonstrated actions while the VLA stays frozen, with continuous gates as a training surrogate and hard routing that drops unselected source tokens.
Fgbe7fEJsv.key_idea: Estimate per-source utility from source representations plus intermediate VLA states, then hard-route to keep only useful source tokens for action prediction while the VLA stays frozen.
Fgbe7fEJsv.evidence: Five VLA configurations on LIBERO-Plus and CALVIN.
Fgbe7fEJsv.claimed_gains: Average relative improvements of 8.58% on LIBERO-Plus and 11.16% on CALVIN while retaining only 45% and 44% of the available source groups for action prediction.

QIfIKZ1qGX.one_liner: Cost-aware experiment selection for research agents using a single online shadow price on compute and a one-box Pandora's box rule.
QIfIKZ1qGX.problem: Existing methods decide one experiment at a time, ignoring that compute given to one experiment is unavailable to later ones whose value is still unknown.
QIfIKZ1qGX.method: Given a shadow price on compute, each candidate is a single-box Pandora's box problem whose exact solution is to skip it, run it in full, or first run a cheap partial version. The price updates online, rising when compute is spent faster than the search moves through candidates and falling otherwise; a parameter-free form of the update admits a distribution-free certificate.
QIfIKZ1qGX.key_idea: Couple per-candidate decisions with one online-updated shadow price on compute, and solve each as a single-box Pandora's problem: skip, run fully, or run partially first.
QIfIKZ1qGX.evidence: Comparison against ten baselines on TabRepo, LCBench, and AIRS-Bench; the abstract is truncated after the certificate.
QIfIKZ1qGX.claimed_gains: With 5 to 40 percent of the full compute, CAES outperforms ten baselines on TabRepo, LCBench and AIRS-Bench.

1bjuVsKVni.one_liner: Latent action model splitting synchronized multi-view context into shared global and view-private components for selective cross-view sharing.
1bjuVsKVni.problem: Latent action models mostly use a single camera stream, and multi-view versions stress view invariance even though synchronized cameras give complementary, not interchangeable, evidence about the same action.
1bjuVsKVni.method: For each target view CARVE forms global components from synchronized multi-view context and keeps target-view private components; a shared future-dynamics model routes global information across views while private information goes only to its own predictor. Training has three stages: single-view pretraining, amplitude-guided multi-view adaptation, and global-private decomposition.
1bjuVsKVni.key_idea: Share transition information across views only through global components, while keeping view-private components restricted to their own target-view predictor.
1bjuVsKVni.evidence: Long-horizon video prediction and downstream robot control against latent action baselines, with representation analyses and ablations.

iIHDAaLD8w.one_liner: Flow-matching DiT for Cell Painting that encodes each fluorescence channel separately with channel and role embeddings across datasets and tasks.
iIHDAaLD8w.problem: Cell Painting datasets differ in channel count, labeled structures, and setup (brightfield, same-batch controls), so a single-dataset model generalizes poorly and a unified model is hard to train.
iIHDAaLD8w.method: OmniMorph is a flow-matching model with a DiT backbone that encodes each fluorescence channel separately. Two embeddings separate a channel's semantics from its role; the channel embedding marks the subcellular structure and is shared across datasets, and the abstract is truncated before describing the second.
iIHDAaLD8w.key_idea: Encode each fluorescence channel separately and disentangle channel identity (a shared structure embedding) from channel role with two embeddings, so one model handles varying channel sets.
iIHDAaLD8w.evidence: The abstract is truncated before experiments; keywords mention morphology generation and perturbation prediction.

npYxMyvOP4.one_liner: Unified MLLM supporting eight physical sensory modalities via language-aligned representations and modality-specific experts, trained on 1M samples.
npYxMyvOP4.problem: Embodied MLLMs perceive mostly vision and audio, and other sensory modalities connect weakly to the MLLM and differ in structure and statistics.
npYxMyvOP4.method: UniSense trains in two stages: aligning sensory representations with language, then tuning modality-specific experts within the shared LLM. It uses UniSense-1M, a corpus of 1M samples across 8 sensory modalities.
npYxMyvOP4.key_idea: Align each sensory modality to language first, then add modality-specific experts within a shared LLM for specialized processing.
npYxMyvOP4.evidence: 12 benchmarks spanning depth, point cloud, IMU, tactile, thermal, radar, motion, and smell understanding.
npYxMyvOP4.claimed_gains: Reports strong performance across 12 benchmarks and outperformance of comparison models that the truncated abstract does not name; no numeric gains are visible.

XUtn5p89iG.one_liner: Benchmark testing whether agents turn general LLM capability into cheap task-specific artifacts under fixed time, compute, and API budgets.
XUtn5p89iG.problem: Querying LLMs separately for millions of related instances is prohibitively expensive, and it is unknown whether agents can autonomously build cheaper solutions, an ability the authors call bottling.
XUtn5p89iG.method: Bottled gives agents an entire unlabelled workload under fixed time, compute, and LLM API budgets; agents choose their own approach, such as training a small model or writing a reusable program, and are judged on answer quality and amortised cost.
XUtn5p89iG.key_idea: Score agents on the quality and amortised cost of the artifact they build for a recurring workload, rather than on zero-shot task performance.
XUtn5p89iG.evidence: Ten models on three tasks (90 runs), compared with zero-shot performance and two naive small-model distillation baselines with the same token budget.
XUtn5p89iG.claimed_gains: 73 of 90 runs score below the lower bound of the 95% confidence interval of their model's zero-shot performance, 46 of 90 underperform the stronger naive distillation baseline, and Opus 5 retains approximately 84% of its zero-shot macro-F1 at roughly 692 times lower reported cost.

naJLzg12fp.one_liner: World-space human mesh recovery that uses feed-forward 3D reconstruction geometry to mediate global translation reasoning for SMPL-X bodies.
naJLzg12fp.problem: Monocular HMR methods recover world-space motion well, but robust global trajectory estimation remains hard under monocular ambiguity.
naJLzg12fp.method: HER uses a backbone-agnostic feed-forward geometry frontend for consistent geometry and camera trajectories, a frozen pretrained image HMR encoder with a learned temporal human representation for SMPL-X and joint prediction, and a geometry-mediated spatial reasoner for global translation. Body structure supplies a scale reference, and a lightweight world-space optimizer improves temporal and contact consistency.
naJLzg12fp.key_idea: Couple the temporal human representation with the human geometry recovered by feed-forward reconstruction in a learned spatial reasoner that predicts temporally consistent global translation.
naJLzg12fp.evidence: Experiments on EMDB2 and RICH; the abstract is truncated before the numbers.
naJLzg12fp.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract only says HER outperforms prior methods in world-space human reconstruction while keeping strong local accuracy.

M6DeF9lL99.one_liner: Training-free decoder overlaps adjacent-block decoding in diffusion VLMs and remasks only stale draft tokens via token-to-token verification.
M6DeF9lL99.problem: Long-form generation in diffusion MLLMs is bottlenecked by serial dependencies across blocks, and an early-started successor block can be invalidated when its unstable predecessor context is updated.
M6DeF9lL99.method: VisWave overlaps the decoding of adjacent blocks through revisable wavefront execution. Virtual-remask token-to-token verification (VR-T2T) re-evaluates affected draft tokens under the latest textual and visual context; supported tokens are kept and the rest are remasked and returned to native denoising.
M6DeF9lL99.key_idea: Start the next block early on an unstable context, then re-verify and remask only the few draft tokens that changed, since most successor tokens remain reusable.
M6DeF9lL99.evidence: Seven natural workloads with BARD-VL-4B as the named base model; the abstract is truncated after the first speedup figure.
M6DeF9lL99.claimed_gains: The TL;DR states up to 2.07× speedup with task quality preserved, and the abstract reports 1.57× on BARD-VL-4B across seven natural workloads (text truncated).

ck9F16zS9F.one_liner: Unified on-policy distillation recipe balancing student data exposure and calibrating teacher token guidance to outcome reward.
ck9F16zS9F.problem: The conditions under which on-policy distillation reliably improves a student are poorly understood; the authors identify insufficient informative-state exposure and unreliable teacher supervision on student rollouts as two bottlenecks.
ck9F16zS9F.method: On the student side, offline and online data balancing raises informative-state exposure. On the teacher side, an outcome-guided margin calibration restores order-consistency between aggregated token-level guidance and the outcome reward for correct versus incorrect trajectories.
ck9F16zS9F.key_idea: Calibrate teacher token-level guidance with an outcome-guided margin so aggregated guidance ranks correct above incorrect trajectories, while balancing offline and online data for the student.
ck9F16zS9F.evidence: 16 benchmarks across 5 domains for both LLMs and MLLMs, covering single-teacher, multi-teacher, strong-to-weak, and cross-modal distillation settings.
ck9F16zS9F.claimed_gains: Average gain of 2.1 points over vanilla OPD.

a04zOP6ZLu.one_liner: 0.5B Mixture-of-Transformers robot policy learns action-grounded latents via masked inverse and forward dynamics, then flow-matching action generation.
a04zOP6ZLu.problem: Compact manipulation policies need representations that capture how actions change observations, but large multimodal backbones and pixel-level world models spend computation on details beyond what control needs.
a04zOP6ZLu.method: A Mixture-of-Transformers jointly models observation latents and continuous action tokens. Stage 1 uses masked trajectory prediction (reconstruct actions from current and future observations; predict future visual representations from current observations and actions with an EMA target encoder), and stage 2 trains the shared backbone for action generation with flow matching, needing no future observations at deployment.
a04zOP6ZLu.key_idea: Learn inverse-dynamics action reconstruction and EMA-targeted forward latent prediction inside the same backbone that later generates actions, with no pixel reconstruction or inference-time rollouts.
a04zOP6ZLu.evidence: LIBERO, CALVIN, and zero-shot LIBERO-Plus, plus comparison with pi_0.5 and Fast-WAM in average task progress (abstract truncated).
a04zOP6ZLu.claimed_gains: 0.47B trainable policy parameters, competitive performance on LIBERO and CALVIN, 77.45% success on zero-shot LIBERO-Plus, and higher average task progress than pi_0.5 and Fast-WAM.

5El1iP7YPo.one_liner: Maintains separate latent reasoning trajectories and sets branching width at inference using collision probabilities from output-token distributions.
5El1iP7YPo.problem: In continuous latent reasoning, a single branch can act as a lossless implicit beam only if its state preserves distinctions between beams that need different futures, which a shared state may not do.
5El1iP7YPo.method: COCONUT Tree keeps distinct latent trajectories from separate initial proposals and adjusts reasoning width at inference. Collision probabilities from the output-token distribution drive a stopping rule that optimizes a penalised local coverage surrogate, with maximum branching width B_max as the only hyperparameter and no training or calibration.
5El1iP7YPo.key_idea: Branch latent reasoning into separate trajectories and stop adding paths via a collision-probability bound that exactly optimizes a penalised local coverage surrogate.
5El1iP7YPo.evidence: COCONUT, CODI, and COLAR in 24 evaluated settings against an equal-compute shared-state control, plus live inference timing on COCONUT.
5El1iP7YPo.claimed_gains: Distinct initial proposals improve coverage in all 24 evaluated settings, and adaptive branching cuts wall-clock time by 13.6--60.0% on COCONUT (the FLOPs figure is truncated).

ChmQ3Uw7zI.one_liner: GRPO-trained attacker planner synthesizes multi-turn text-and-image-operation jailbreak plans for queries whose harmful answers depend on image content.
ChmQ3Uw7zI.problem: Multimodal red teaming mostly uses images as wrappers for malicious payloads, leaving the case where the image itself supplies the information for an image-specific harmful answer unstudied.
ChmQ3Uw7zI.method: They formalize Visual Exclusivity (VE) and propose MM-Plan, which trains an attacker planner with GRPO to synthesize whole multi-turn strategies (text queries plus predefined visual operations) without human-annotated attack trajectories. They also release VE-Safety, 440 human-curated instances across 15 safety categories.
ChmQ3Uw7zI.key_idea: Replace turn-by-turn reactive jailbreaking with global plan synthesis, training a planner via GRPO to choose text queries and predefined visual operations.
ChmQ3Uw7zI.evidence: Eight MLLMs evaluated on the VE-Safety dataset against compared baselines.
ChmQ3Uw7zI.claimed_gains: 46.3% attack success against Claude 4.5 Sonnet and 13.8% against GPT-5, outperforming the compared baselines across eight MLLMs.

IwgY4l6lax.one_liner: Backprop-free test-time adapter for VLMs that corrects frozen logits using streaming feature-posterior cross-covariance.
IwgY4l6lax.problem: Cache-based TTA methods keep confidence-selected examples or hard pseudo-labels that discard target evidence and propagate errors, while distributional methods need costly covariance state or sensitive hyperparameters.
IwgY4l6lax.method: ACME keeps exact streaming feature and posterior statistics together with their cross-covariance, using the full frozen posterior of every test sample, and derives class-specific directions for a bounded residual correction to the frozen logits. It needs no source data, stored test samples, or full class-conditional covariance matrices.
IwgY4l6lax.key_idea: Accumulate exact streaming cross-covariance between features and the full frozen posterior, and convert it into class-specific directions for a bounded residual logit correction.
IwgY4l6lax.evidence: Distribution-shift and cross-dataset benchmarks (specific datasets are not visible in the abstract).
IwgY4l6lax.claimed_gains: Additional GPU memory of 3 MiB and the highest inference throughput among the evaluated methods; no accuracy numbers are stated.

7a5Nv6uSPB.one_liner: Driving VLA trained with negative and recovery trajectories via NR-RFT and a flow-matching action bridge on sparse-layer KV caches.
7a5Nv6uSPB.problem: Driving VLAs are trained only on positive expert demonstrations, giving little supervision on which behaviors to avoid or how to recover from failures, which limits robustness.
7a5Nv6uSPB.method: They build nuReasoning-NR (36K reasoning-intensive scenarios, including 3K suboptimal and 3K expert recovery trajectories) and train with Negative-Recovery Reinforcement Fine-Tuning, which penalizes undesirable behavior, rewards expert corrective actions, and adds an advantage correction for groups of similar suboptimal rollouts. SpanVLA keeps autoregressive reasoning and adds a lightweight flow-matching action bridge conditioned on sparse-layer KV caches and initialized from the historical trajectory.
7a5Nv6uSPB.key_idea: Use asymmetric RL rewards that penalize suboptimal trajectories and reward expert recovery, and generate actions via a flow-matching bridge initialized from the historical trajectory.
7a5Nv6uSPB.evidence: Experiments on NAVSIM v1/v2, nuReasoning, and further benchmarks (abstract truncated).

yNnjQDCNj4.one_liner: Test-time agentic runtime adds perception skills, rule-based action verification, and feedback-driven recovery planning to existing driving experts.
yNnjQDCNj4.problem: End-to-end driving policies accumulate closed-loop errors, especially in unseen scenarios, and can reach states from which the same policy cannot recover.
yNnjQDCNj4.method: AUTOAGENT0 wraps an existing driving expert with an independent detection module that builds scene context from complementary perception skills and a rule-based verifier that checks action feasibility. When nominal trajectories are unreliable, the orchestrator activates Recovery Planning, an agentic loop that composes alternative maneuvers from action primitives and refines them with verification feedback.
yNnjQDCNj4.key_idea: Treat closed-loop safety as test-time execution: verify the expert's action with rules and, on failure, iteratively compose and refine maneuvers from action primitives using verifier feedback.
yNnjQDCNj4.evidence: Evaluations are mentioned, but the abstract is truncated before naming benchmarks or models.

ZkDoKsCCMH.one_liner: Proves a stratified metric-entropy law for infinite-width ReLU^k networks, where parameter smoothness may degrade on a positive-codimension set.
ZkDoKsCCMH.problem: The metric entropy of infinite-width ReLU^k classes depends on data through an anti-concentration (margin) exponent, and imposing that margin law uniformly over parameters predicts a degradation that can be an artifact of the uniformity.
ZkDoKsCCMH.method: They show the margin exponent can never exceed one, then prove a stratified entropy law in which parameter smoothness may fall off at a controlled rate on a set of positive codimension; the entropy exponent is governed by the better of two competing terms and reduces to the Siegel and Xu (2024) smooth-dictionary bound when the bad set is everything.
ZkDoKsCCMH.key_idea: Replace a uniform margin assumption with a stratified one in which smoothness of the parameter-to-feature map degrades only on a positive-codimension set, such as boundaries tangent to a data manifold.
ZkDoKsCCMH.evidence: Theoretical results (a bound on the margin exponent and the stratified entropy law) with data on a curved low-dimensional manifold as the motivating case; the abstract is truncated.

bYTx2ULAGC.one_liner: Converts sparse outcomes into step-level rewards by backtracking from the answer to clues, for SFT and GRPO of search agents.
bYTx2ULAGC.problem: Training for long-horizon search agents treats all steps in a trajectory uniformly in both SFT and RL, so useful actions are not distinguished from erroneous or redundant ones.
bYTx2ULAGC.method: ABC recovers the intermediate clues a query needs by tracing back from its ground-truth answer (Answer-Backtracked Clue Recovery), then scores each search step against those clues (Clue-Anchored Step Scoring). ABC-SFT reweights each turn's loss with the scores and ABC-GRPO uses them as step-level rewards; ABSeeker is trained on Qwen3.5-4B.
bYTx2ULAGC.key_idea: Backtrack from the ground-truth answer to the clues a solution needs, then score each search step against those clues to give dense step-level credit, even in failed trajectories.
bYTx2ULAGC.evidence: ABSeeker is trained from Qwen3.5-4B with only 8.5k (unit cut off in the abstract); the abstract is truncated before any results.

hGr6OfrAUe.one_liner: Causal interventions on hidden-state changes show text-learned facts still influence speech-model answers when spoken recall fails.
hGr6OfrAUe.problem: A speech language model can learn a fact from text and answer it in writing yet fail on the same spoken question, and it is unclear whether the information is absent, present but unused, or used but insufficient.
hGr6OfrAUe.method: They teach models new facts via text-only fine-tuning, then change the learned answers and selectively remove the resulting hidden-state changes while the model processes speech, to test whether those changes carry answer content and affect generation.
hGr6OfrAUe.key_idea: Compare ablating the hidden-state changes tied to the queried fact against removing equally strong changes tied to other facts, and amplify the changes beyond original strength.
hGr6OfrAUe.evidence: Two model families, varied question wording and synthesized voices, and a controlled amplification ablation on speech failures.
hGr6OfrAUe.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports qualitative findings only (content-sensitive harm from removal, little improvement from amplification).

GUe8parm8V.one_liner: Redistributes trajectory-level outcome advantage across agent decisions with bounded mean-one weights from process guidance, preserving sign and mean.
GUe8parm8V.problem: Outcome-based RL gives every intermediate decision the same trajectory-level advantage, while process supervision used as a separate objective can push decisions against the outcome advantage, and self-distillation guidance does not specify how to allocate outcome credit.
GUe8parm8V.method: TASPO lets outcome feedback set the trajectory-level advantage and uses process supervision only to redistribute it across decisions. It aligns guidance from verified successful sibling trajectories with the target interaction, measures guidance-induced support over executable actions, and converts the scores into positive, bounded, mean-one weights without extra environment interaction.
GUe8parm8V.key_idea: Constrained credit redistribution: reweight each decision's share of the outcome advantage with positive, bounded, mean-one weights so advantage sign and per-trajectory mean are preserved.
GUe8parm8V.evidence: Evaluated on ALFWorld, Search-QA, and further settings (abstract truncated).

ddUktvl59g.one_liner: Two-stage GRPO enhancement: semantic-entropy-triggered expert prefixes restore advantage variance, and Renyi preconditioning reaches confident wrong tokens.
ddUktvl59g.problem: RL's effect on hallucination in MLLMs is uneven: hard queries often yield unanimously wrong rollout groups so group-relative advantage collapses to zero, and confident-but-wrong tokens receive vanishing gradients as the policy sharpens.
ddUktvl59g.method: DEEPO injects grounded expert-prefix continuations on high semantic-entropy queries to provide supervision and restore advantage variance, and applies advantage-sign-aware Renyi preconditioning to counter logit-level saturation so correction reaches confident errors.
ddUktvl59g.key_idea: Inject expert prefixes where semantic entropy is high to revive zero-variance GRPO groups, and precondition gradients with advantage-sign-aware Renyi scaling to counter saturation on confident errors.
ddUktvl59g.evidence: Ablations of the two branches against GRPO on a multimodal evaluation suite that includes VideoMMMU (abstract truncated).
ddUktvl59g.claimed_gains: Both branches improve over GRPO individually; their interaction on VideoMMMU is +4.0 (95% CI [1.1, 6.9]).

Pzjb5xauNP.one_liner: Continual phrase-to-patch alignment: learns counterfactually supervised mixture anchors, freezes them, and selects local evidence by density, concentration, and stability.
Pzjb5xauNP.problem: Continual VLM methods check global predictions and image-text stability but not whether the model keeps the local patch evidence needed to ground a phrase; a global decision can stay stable while its supporting patch evidence drifts or diffuses.
Pzjb5xauNP.method: CIRCE learns stable phrase-conditioned mixture anchors using counterfactual supervision, spatial compactness, and perturbation stability, then freezes the acquired local state. For an image and target phrase it selects the retained state with the strongest mixture density, spatial concentration, and prediction stability.
Pzjb5xauNP.key_idea: Store phrase-conditioned mixture anchors trained with counterfactual, compactness, and perturbation-stability terms, freeze them per stage, and pick among retained states by density, concentration, and stability.
Pzjb5xauNP.evidence: Experiments on COCO80-CI8 and VG16-CI4 against representative continual learning baselines.
Pzjb5xauNP.claimed_gains: Superior Grounded Counterfactual Accuracy and better preservation of local phrase-region evidence than representative continual learning baselines; no numbers are stated.

aMNygSxgNJ.one_liner: Training-free change localization: selects a few LVLM attention heads by deviation from an unchanged baseline, then refines with SAM.
aMNygSxgNJ.problem: LVLMs can describe changes between images but localize them poorly, while localization-only methods find changes but cannot say what they are.
aMNygSxgNJ.method: They select attention heads (at most 0.7% of all heads) by their attention-sum deviation from an unchanged self-reference baseline and their spatial consistency across both image directions, diffuse head attention through semantic affinities from the frozen vision encoder, and feed the resulting maps to SAM refinement.
aMNygSxgNJ.key_idea: A small subset of frozen-LVLM attention heads already encodes change evidence; identify them by self-reference deviation and bidirectional spatial consistency, with no pixel-level supervision.
aMNygSxgNJ.evidence: Diverse change localization benchmarks (names not visible in the abstract), compared with LVLM-based baselines and localization-only approaches.
aMNygSxgNJ.claimed_gains: Substantially surpasses LVLM-based baselines and matches dedicated localization-only approaches while using at most 0.7% of attention heads; no benchmark numbers are stated.

Y72FuSUQ7h.one_liner: Video world model storing scene memory in HexMemory, six fixed-size feature planes updated by a feed-forward writer.
Y72FuSUQ7h.problem: Existing spatial memories for video world models accumulate RGB observations or latent features, so storage grows as generation proceeds.
Y72FuSUQ7h.method: HexMemory is a low-rank representation with six spatial and spatiotemporal planes. A feed-forward writer maps each generated chunk into plane features; previous planes are warped while keeping their dimensions and fused with new features by confidence-weighted pooling and a learned residual correction, and a reader retrieves latents to condition later generation.
Y72FuSUQ7h.key_idea: Keep scene memory in six fixed-size spatial and spatiotemporal feature planes that are warped and fused with each new chunk via confidence-weighted pooling, so storage does not grow.
Y72FuSUQ7h.evidence: Experiments on WorldScore and RealEstate10K evaluating video generation quality and revisit consistency.
Y72FuSUQ7h.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract claims strong generation quality, robust revisit consistency, and constant feature storage, with no numbers.

5fhkI7DmvK.one_liner: Geometry-aware low-rank compression of feed-forward 3D reconstruction transformers, allocating rank by geometric sensitivity with adaptive refinement.
5fhkI7DmvK.problem: Feed-forward visual geometry transformers have large backbones with high compute and memory cost, and existing efficiency work reduces spatial-token redundancy but not channel-space redundancy.
5fhkI7DmvK.method: GeoRank builds low-rank operators by activation-aware factorization in a calibration stage and redistributes a rank budget according to geometric sensitivity. During training it adds lightweight adaptive refinement that adjusts the compressed representation per input and restores information lost to truncation, plus geometry-sensitive regularization; the factorized form also supports streaming inference by caching historical features compactly.
5fhkI7DmvK.key_idea: Factorize encoder and decoder operators with activation-aware low-rank decomposition and allocate the rank budget by geometric sensitivity rather than activation energy alone.
5fhkI7DmvK.evidence: Not visible; the abstract is truncated before the experiments.

hIA7FFZytr.one_liner: SE(3)-equivariant object-centric keypose predictor guides a frozen keypose-conditioned VLA for one-shot adaptation to new manipulation tasks.
hIA7FFZytr.problem: A generalist VLA may recognize task-relevant objects and reuse motor skills yet fail to infer the precise 3D configurations needed when only one demonstration of a new task is available.
hIA7FFZytr.method: EquiKey learns from a single demonstration to infer a sparse sequence of task-relevant keyposes, which are temporally scheduled as high-level geometric targets for the frozen, pretrained EquiKey-VLA; that policy generates dense continuous actions conditioned on the latest observation.
hIA7FFZytr.key_idea: Predict sparse object-centric SE(3)-equivariant keyposes from one demonstration and feed them as scheduled geometric targets to a pretrained keypose-conditioned VLA, leaving the backbone untouched.
hIA7FFZytr.evidence: 10 one-shot OOD tasks in RoboTwin 2.0 (Easy and Hard settings) and real-world one-shot Task-OOD experiments.
hIA7FFZytr.claimed_gains: Average success of 77.1% (Easy) and 76.9% (Hard) on RoboTwin 2.0, improving the strongest VLA baseline by 42.5% and 44.6% and the strongest one-shot adaptation baseline by 26.5% and 33.6%; 73.3% success in real-world experiments (text truncated).

IUKnax4deH.one_liner: Outcome-aware security auditor for LLM multi-agent systems that separates attack exposure from realized compromise, with graph-grounded attribution.
IUKnax4deH.problem: Existing MAS defenses cover access control, anomaly detection, or task-failure prediction separately and lack a unified way to decide whether an attack actually compromised the system, where, and on what evidence.
IUKnax4deH.method: MOSAIC integrates attack detection, realized-outcome assessment, structural localization, and evidence-grounded attribution. It comes with MOSAIC-Bench, a benchmark that distinguishes attack exposure from realized compromise, and MOSAIC-Auditor, a graph-grounded auditor that reasons over multi-agent execution trajectories.
IUKnax4deH.key_idea: Audit execution trajectories with a graph-grounded reasoner that separates attack exposure from realized compromise and attributes the effect to specific structural locations with evidence.
IUKnax4deH.evidence: Experiments on MOSAIC-Bench; the abstract gives no datasets, models, or numbers.

5aV8NnvjaO.one_liner: Learns shared and modality-specific latent affective units through iterative soft assignment to localize emotion segments in multimodal sequences.
5aV8NnvjaO.problem: Cross-modal temporal misalignment and sparse affective cues make existing fusion methods introduce redundant or unreliable information when localizing emotion-bearing segments in untrimmed multimodal sequences.
5aV8NnvjaO.method: LLAU learns shared and modality-specific units and iteratively refines soft token-to-unit assignments and unit representations using cross-modal support, semantic affinity, and temporal affinity; the assignments act as affective priors for reconstructing dense features along the original timeline and guide modality-specific experts in weighting residual features. The paper also introduces EmoTEL-8, a target-centric benchmark with visual, acoustic, and textual modalities.
5aV8NnvjaO.key_idea: Cluster sparse multimodal tokens into temporally structured latent units using cross-modal, semantic, and temporal affinity, then use the assignments as priors to reconstruct dense, boundary-sensitive features.
5aV8NnvjaO.evidence: Evaluation on the EmoTEL-8 benchmark; the abstract is truncated before results.

AeVdTLO0lB.one_liner: Training-free zero-shot anomaly detection that reverses score polarity of CLIP's frozen visual projector and keeps principal singular directions.
AeVdTLO0lB.problem: CLIP-based zero-shot anomaly detection usually relies on prompts or adapters trained on auxiliary data, and transfer to unseen domains remains unreliable.
AeVdTLO0lB.method: 0-CLIP converts CLIP's frozen visual projector into a patch-to-text anomaly operator by reversing the normal-abnormal score polarity, forming a compact operator from the principal singular directions, and selectively recovering lower-energy directions with a separation criterion computed on the first unlabeled test image of each category. It produces pixel-level anomaly maps and image-level scores without labeled data.
AeVdTLO0lB.key_idea: CLIP's frozen visual projector holds dense anomaly structure with inverted polarity; flip it and pick its singular directions with a separation criterion from one unlabeled test image per category.
AeVdTLO0lB.evidence: Industrial and medical anomaly detection benchmarks with ablation studies (specific datasets are not visible).
AeVdTLO0lB.claimed_gains: Performance competitive with training-based methods; no numbers are stated.

rYuDrS2PWT.one_liner: Post-trains driving world action models with trajectory GRPO and simulator-rendered future videos matched to sampled trajectories.
rYuDrS2PWT.problem: Driving logs contain future videos only for the recorded trajectory, so alternative trajectories explored during RL post-training have no matching visual supervision.
rYuDrS2PWT.method: For each observation SimVTA samples candidate trajectories and renders future videos for high-reward ones with a real-world simulator (e.g., World Engine) over 3DGS-reconstructed scenes, prioritizing higher-error futures under a rendering budget. It optimizes planning with group-relative trajectory optimization plus a flow-matching loss on the matched videos that updates shared representations; inference predicts trajectories directly without simulator calls.
rYuDrS2PWT.key_idea: Render simulator videos for sampled high-reward trajectories and train a video flow-matching loss on them alongside trajectory GRPO so shared representations carry video supervision into planning.
rYuDrS2PWT.evidence: NAVSIM v1, NAVSIM v2, and a third benchmark reporting HD-Score (name truncated in the abstract).
rYuDrS2PWT.claimed_gains: On NAVSIM v1, PDMS rises from 86.2 to 91.3 (a gain of 5.1 points); 88.2 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2 and an average HD-Score of 37.3.

PJ0r1ncVMs.one_liner: Agentic loop that proposes, diagnoses, and revises first-order-logic hypotheses over knowledge graphs to explain observed entities.
PJ0r1ncVMs.problem: One-shot controllable hypothesis generators can output well-formed hypotheses that satisfy the conditions yet fail to explain the observed entities, with no mechanism to detect or fix the mismatch.
PJ0r1ncVMs.method: A Hypothesis Proposal Agent calls a small trained generator; root-cause analysis uses fragment-level coverage to locate branches to inspect and gathers neighborhood evidence from the training graph; a Hypothesis Refiner Agent combines this diagnosis with earlier hypotheses to produce updated conditions and directly revised hypotheses.
PJ0r1ncVMs.key_idea: Treat condition signals as operators that steer generation, and close the abductive loop by locating failing branches via fragment-level coverage and having a refiner agent revise them.
PJ0r1ncVMs.evidence: BioKG, PharmKG8k, and DBpedia50 in single-turn and multi-turn settings, compared with one-shot generation.
PJ0r1ncVMs.claimed_gains: Outperforms one-shot generation on BioKG, PharmKG8k, and DBpedia50 in single-turn and multi-turn settings; no numbers are visible in the abstract.

aAHWylKrLU.one_liner: Offline RL with multiple one-step IMLE generators, ensemble-agreement filtering, and action selection by an independently learned value function.
aAHWylKrLU.problem: Offline datasets have multimodal behavior distributions that are hard to model and risk out-of-distribution actions, and diffusion- or flow-based policies address this at the cost of iterative generation, distillation, or auxiliary optimization.
aAHWylKrLU.method: VIMLE uses multiple conditional IMLE generators for one-step parallel action generation, filters unreliable candidates by ensemble agreement, and selects high-value actions with a separately learned value function, avoiding multi-step generation and auxiliary policy training.
aAHWylKrLU.key_idea: Generate candidate actions in one step from several conditional IMLE generators, keep those the ensemble agrees on, and choose the highest-value one using a decoupled value function.
aAHWylKrLU.evidence: D4RL benchmarks, compared with diffusion-based approaches on training time and inference latency.
aAHWylKrLU.claimed_gains: Competitive performance across D4RL tasks with substantially lower training time and inference latency than diffusion-based approaches; no numbers are stated.

jLGEqjSjgI.one_liner: Decouples localization and segmentation features by word-guided routing, then couples them with sentence and mask priors on a frozen encoder.
jLGEqjSjgI.problem: Multi-task visual grounding methods enforce cooperation through shared representations and overlook the conflict between the feature interests of localization and segmentation.
jLGEqjSjgI.method: Task-aware Semantic Decoupling (TSD) routes shared visual cues into task-specific features under salient word-level guidance; Hybrid Prior Coupling (HPC) integrates a sentence-level semantic prior with a mask-derived spatial prior, since segmentation supplies informative localization priors through dense supervision. Built on a frozen multimodal encoder, it trains only lightweight parameters.
jLGEqjSjgI.key_idea: First route shared visual cues into separate localization and segmentation features by salient words, then feed mask-derived spatial priors plus sentence-level semantics back to improve grounding.
jLGEqjSjgI.evidence: Experiments on multiple grounding objectives; benchmarks are not visible because the abstract is truncated.

ONzfXsihD3.one_liner: Recovers a subliminally transferred trait direction from distillation parameter updates alone, using its consistency across teacher datasets.
ONzfXsihD3.problem: A student distilled from a teacher with the same base parameters can inherit the teacher's traits, including misalignment, from semantically unrelated data, and all existing defences require knowing the trait.
ONzfXsihD3.method: They prove a transferred trait can be recovered from parameter updates without supervision by exploiting that it is expressed consistently across diverse teacher-generated datasets while task-specific and shared capabilities vary. The estimator returns a weight-space direction that can be amplified to discover and interpret the trait or projected out to suppress it.
ONzfXsihD3.key_idea: Find the weight-space direction that is consistent across updates from diverse teacher datasets, then amplify it to inspect the trait or project it out to suppress it.
ONzfXsihD3.evidence: A proof of recoverability from parameter updates, and application to the subliminal-learning benchmarks of Cloud et al., 2026.
ONzfXsihD3.claimed_gains: Recovers the transmitted animal-preference traits without trait labels and suppresses their expression with almost no impact on task performance; no numbers are stated.

mmUlhcO6H1.one_liner: Training-based video concept unlearning that localizes and edits concept-related representations while a preservation objective keeps the non-target scene.
mmUlhcO6H1.problem: Existing unlearning for video generators targets static concepts, largely ignores motion, and often alters the background, composition, or dynamics when removing the target.
mmUlhcO6H1.method: FOMO is built around two objectives, what to change and what to preserve: it localizes concept-related representations and modifies them, while a preservation mechanism maintains non-target scene information without auxiliary data.
mmUlhcO6H1.key_idea: Localize the representations tied to the target concept for modification and add a preservation term that keeps non-target scene information, with no auxiliary data needed.
mmUlhcO6H1.evidence: Not visible; the abstract is truncated before the experiments.

1n4L8nXB1I.one_liner: Builds a 103,707-pair real-world restoration dataset using Nano-Banana-2 outputs as generative ground truth with multi-stage quality control.
1n4L8nXB1I.problem: Real-world image restoration lacks high-quality paired training data: synthetic data misses real degradations and real paired data is expensive to capture, so trained models generalize poorly.
1n4L8nXB1I.method: They evaluate nine multimodal foundation models, find Nano-Banana-2 with VLM-based adaptive prompting best at producing realistic, content-faithful HQ targets from real LQ images, and use it in a synthesis pipeline with multi-stage quality control to build GGT-100K (103,707 training pairs) plus a 500-pair test set.
1n4L8nXB1I.key_idea: Use a generative multimodal foundation model's output on a real low-quality image as its high-quality target, with VLM-adaptive prompting and multi-stage quality filtering.
1n4L8nXB1I.evidence: A systematic comparison of nine multimodal foundation models and experiments on a wide range of IR models trained on GGT-100K (abstract truncated).
1n4L8nXB1I.claimed_gains: GGT-100K consistently improves real-world generalization of a wide range of IR models (numbers truncated in the abstract); the dataset has 103,707 training pairs and a 500-pair test set.

7HpKzk9OZm.one_liner: Curates a balanced 27k-video open-domain super-resolution dataset and proposes GraCo-VSR, a reliability-aware one-step video restoration model.
7HpKzk9OZm.problem: Existing open-domain VSR training datasets are semantically imbalanced and insufficiently diverse, which limits temporally coherent detail across varied scenes and subjects.
7HpKzk9OZm.method: The SCOPE pipeline combines task-oriented video selection with hierarchical semantic rebalancing to build SCOPE-VSR (about 27k videos) and SCOPE-test. GraCo-VSR is a one-step restoration framework with a reliability-aware design and explicit supervision to reduce degradation-induced distortions in motion and texture guidance.
7HpKzk9OZm.key_idea: Rebalance video selection hierarchically by semantics for training data, and supervise the reliability of motion and texture guidance explicitly in a one-step restorer.
7HpKzk9OZm.evidence: Evaluations on SCOPE-test; the abstract names no baselines or metrics.
7HpKzk9OZm.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract only reports strong reconstruction fidelity and perceptual quality.

fgf0qKhzVI.one_liner: Two-stage text-to-video: flow model generates latent world states in V-JEPA space, then a second flow renders them in VAE space.
fgf0qKhzVI.problem: Representation-space video generation is underexplored, and the high dimensionality of video representations makes diffusion-transformer denoising difficult.
fgf0qKhzVI.method: WorldFlow separates world-state modeling from rendering: a text-conditioned flow model generates latent world states in native V-JEPA space, and a second flow model renders them into videos in VAE space. Riemannian Flow Matching on the native representation manifold with v-prediction models the high-dimensional representations without extra compression.
fgf0qKhzVI.key_idea: Generate semantic world states in the native V-JEPA representation using Riemannian flow matching with v-prediction, then render appearance in VAE space with a second flow model.
fgf0qKhzVI.evidence: Large-scale open-domain text-to-video generation with a systematic study of representation geometry and prediction parameterization; results are truncated.

HsJfkHweWm.one_liner: DOFTRL-GT combines delay-compensated optimism with two-level gradient tracking over accelerated gossip for gradient-variation and small-loss regret.
HsJfkHweWm.problem: Existing decentralized online convex optimization algorithms reach near-optimal worst-case regret but do not adapt to benign loss sequences with small gradient variation or small comparator loss.
HsJfkHweWm.method: DOFTRL-GT (Decentralized Optimistic Follow-the-Regularized-Leader with Gradient Tracking) runs over a fixed network of N learners with spectral gap rho that communicate only with neighbors. The paper also proves lower bounds matching the upper bounds up to logarithmic factors in their regimes.
HsJfkHweWm.key_idea: Optimistic FTRL with delay compensation and two-level gradient tracking via accelerated gossip lets regret scale with gradient variation V_T or best-comparator loss F_T.
HsJfkHweWm.evidence: Theoretical regret upper bounds and matching lower bounds, plus applications to offline optimization (abstract truncated).
HsJfkHweWm.claimed_gains: Regret of O~(N min{rho^{-3/4} sqrt(V_T), rho^{-1/4} sqrt(F_T)}) for convex losses and O~(N rho^{-1/2} log(2+min{V_T,F_T})) for strongly convex losses, up to additive terms independent of T, V_T, and F_T.

a2tK9x6aOt.one_liner: Builds constrained generative models from Brenier maps, subsuming mirror maps and handling non-convex domains via anchor sampling and smoothing.
a2tK9x6aOt.problem: Analytical mirror functions only work for specific convex domains without a unified construction, and neural approximate mirror functions bring uncontrolled geometric distortion and heavy training overhead.
a2tK9x6aOt.method: They prove mirror functions on convex domains are a special case of dual Brenier functions and use singular set theory to extend to arbitrary convex and non-convex domains. A multi-stage Brenier-map solver uses anchor sampling and geometric variational principles to capture geometry, with a controllable smoothing mechanism to preserve key geometric properties and improve generalization.
a2tK9x6aOt.key_idea: Treat mirror functions as special cases of dual Brenier functions, use singular set theory to drop convexity, and solve the map with anchor sampling and smoothing.
a2tK9x6aOt.evidence: Three classical convex constraint domains against neural approximation baselines, plus a watermark image generation task and five other complex tasks (abstract truncated).
a2tK9x6aOt.claimed_gains: Better fitting accuracy for mirror functions than neural approximation baselines on three classical convex constraint domains; no numbers are stated.

5YJUpxrumD.one_liner: Two-stage post-training for video temporal grounding: self-generated-start SFT, then GRPO that compares end rewards only within the same start.
5YJUpxrumD.problem: Autoregressive video temporal grounding models predict ends much worse than starts, and teacher-forced SFT (prefix exposure bias) and holistic GRPO (which penalizes good ends that follow a poor start) do not teach recovery from a flawed start.
5YJUpxrumD.method: Online-start SFT exposes end prediction to the model's own generated contexts. Conditional-tree GRPO restructures sampling so end rewards are centered only within the same-start branch, isolating conditional end quality from the inherited start penalty.
5YJUpxrumD.key_idea: Group end-prediction rewards by shared start in a sampling tree so GRPO advantage reflects only how well the end continues from that start.
5YJUpxrumD.evidence: TimeLens-Bench, with comparisons to closed-source models and a test forcing continuation from imperfect starts (abstract truncated).
5YJUpxrumD.claimed_gains: FinishStrong-9B reaches 61.7% overall IoU on TimeLens-Bench, above the closed-source Gemini-3.8-Flash and Qwen3.8-Max as stated; the reduction under imperfect starts is truncated.

I5CQFZWM7f.one_liner: Frozen-backbone draft-and-verify acceleration for generative perception using token and trajectory drafters.
I5CQFZWM7f.problem: Generative perception models call the full backbone repeatedly, for autoregressive decoding of detection sequences and iterative denoising of dense maps, which makes inference expensive.
I5CQFZWM7f.method: With the backbone frozen, a token drafter proposes several future tokens and a trajectory drafter proposes future denoising velocities with per-offset error estimates that select a trusted horizon. The backbone then verifies the proposals in one call, so fewer backbone calls are needed.
I5CQFZWM7f.key_idea: Exploit the predictable structure of perception outputs: draft several future tokens or denoising velocities with lightweight drafters and verify them in a single backbone pass.
I5CQFZWM7f.evidence: Multiple generative perception models on detection, panoptic segmentation, depth, and further dense tasks (abstract truncated).
I5CQFZWM7f.claimed_gains: End-to-end speedups of up to 1.6×, 2.0×, 6.3×, and 5.4× on detection, panoptic segmentation, depth, and a fourth task cut off in the abstract.

trkUmQKK4W.one_liner: World-action model that learns manipulation by predicting pixel-aligned 3D point-trajectory motion maps instead of future video frames.
trkUmQKK4W.problem: World-action models' predictive objectives mostly emphasize visual appearance rather than the scene motion relevant to control.
trkUmQKK4W.method: M-WAM predicts pixel-aligned 3D point trajectories organized as image-like motion maps with a pretrained image-generation backbone, jointly optimizing motion and action objectives on shared scene features. Dense trajectories are reconstructed on demand from per-frame simulator geometry, cutting export and storage cost from quadratic to linear in episode length, and the policy generates actions directly at deployment.
trkUmQKK4W.key_idea: Supervise action learning with dense 3D scene motion maps, jointly optimized with actions on shared features, rather than predicting future appearance.
trkUmQKK4W.evidence: RoboTwin ablations, a LIBERO-Plus comparison with ImageWAM, and three real-robot tasks compared with LingBot-VA.
trkUmQKK4W.claimed_gains: On RoboTwin, 3D motion improves success by 10.9 points over last-frame RGB prediction and 6.9 points over 2D motion; mean success on LIBERO-Plus is 1.7 points above ImageWAM; mean success is twice LingBot-VA's across three real-robot tasks.
