8kTYL2EWCw.one_liner: Loops a frozen vision encoder over multiple question-conditioned iterations inside VLMs, trained and evaluated on the new VisRO tasks.
8kTYL2EWCw.problem: Most VLMs treat the vision encoder as a static, question-independent feature extractor, though different questions may need different visual operations and processing depths.
8kTYL2EWCw.method: AdaLoop adapts visual computation to the question and reuses the encoder's transformations across multiple iterations with the pretrained vision weights frozen. The authors also introduce VisRO, a procedural dataset and generation pipeline for training and evaluating vision-centric reasoning.
8kTYL2EWCw.key_idea: Make the vision encoder recurrent: reapply its frozen transformations several times, conditioned on the question, so visual processing depth adapts per query.
8kTYL2EWCw.evidence: Six VisRO tasks across three VLM families, on in-distribution and out-of-distribution examples, against standard fine-tuning and question-conditioned single-pass baselines with matched training data and optimizer updates.
8kTYL2EWCw.claimed_gains: Outperforms standard fine-tuning and question-conditioned single-pass baselines on six VisRO tasks across three VLM families; no numbers are stated.

dTDhhW11MJ.one_liner: Ranks SAM pseudo-mask candidates by how each splits the frozen DINOv2 hypersphere: angular contrast, appearance-mode coverage, and a frame-contact prior.
dTDhhW11MJ.problem: A student trained on the wrong one of several plausible SAM masks inherits its errors, and choosing among candidates otherwise needs a second large model or a quality head fit on annotated masks.
dTDhhW11MJ.method: SphereTrust scores each candidate mask by the angular contrast between the two sides of the split of normalized DINOv2 patch features and by the coverage of the foreground's appearance modes, plus a spatial prior (contact with the image frame), ranking a pool from frozen features alone in 0.55 s per image.
dTDhhW11MJ.key_idea: Treat a candidate mask as a partition of the frozen DINOv2 patch-feature hypersphere and score its angular contrast and appearance-mode coverage, plus a frame-contact prior, without labels.
dTDhhW11MJ.evidence: Eight SAM and SAM3 candidate pools spanning camouflaged, salient, and dichotomous segmentation and low-light camouflage, compared with published selection rules and labeled adaptations of DSS and UCOD-MKD.
dTDhhW11MJ.claimed_gains: Exceeds the strongest evaluated external baseline on six pools by 1.7 to 9.3 percentage points in mean selected Dice; on the two prompted camouflage pools it is within 0.1 points of the DSS adaptation with a lower catastrophic-error rate.

U3kdZUZRIn.one_liner: Region-level GRPO for diffusion and flow models that aggregates positionwise likelihood ratios over text-attention regions before clipping.
U3kdZUZRIn.problem: In online RL for diffusion and flow models, a single global clipping statistic discards the spatial distribution of local likelihood changes, while per-position clipping does not coordinate related latent positions.
U3kdZUZRIn.method: FlowSAPO builds connected, overlapping regions during rollout from the model's own text attention and freezes them for replay. Within each region, exact positionwise log ratios are aggregated with inverse-coverage weights and exponentiated before clipping, leaving the reward and scalar advantage unchanged.
U3kdZUZRIn.key_idea: Group latent positions into text-attention regions, aggregate their local log ratios with inverse-coverage weights, and clip at the region level.
U3kdZUZRIn.evidence: Gaussian-transition analysis with shared covariance, plus image and video comparisons including GenEval and Wan2.1 OCR (abstract truncated).
U3kdZUZRIn.claimed_gains: GenEval attribute binding rises from 0.86 to 0.96 and All Frame OCR on Wan2.1 from 0.339 to 0.427; the VideoReward gain is truncated.

oP8Y8172xS.one_liner: Teacher-free consistency objective using one Jacobian-vector product to align coordinate and categorical predictions across noise levels in 3D molecule generation.
oP8Y8172xS.problem: Few-step 3D molecule generation degrades when predictions change sharply across noise levels, and consistency training does not naturally extend to chemical structure, which changes in discrete jumps.
oP8Y8172xS.method: From the noisy molecule already used in standard training, one Jacobian-vector product computes how each prediction changes along a shared coordinate-time direction; the coordinate tangent forms a regression target and the categorical tangents form soft probability targets for atom, bond, and charge predictions. These terms are added to the standard denoising loss, leaving the network and sampler unchanged.
oP8Y8172xS.key_idea: Use a single Jacobian-vector product along a coordinate-time direction to form regression and soft-categorical targets that keep predictions consistent across nearby noise levels.
oP8Y8172xS.evidence: Comparison with the same-configuration VEDA-FS baseline (benchmark names are truncated in the abstract).
oP8Y8172xS.claimed_gains: Reduces Frechet ChemNet Distance from 4.15 to 0.99 relative to the VEDA-FS baseline (dataset truncated).

eOJ0a5YRoZ.one_liner: Video benchmark for social proactive intelligence built on a four-level world-state taxonomy and 100K+ human annotations.
eOJ0a5YRoZ.problem: Prior social proactive intelligence work uses static images, missing dynamic cues in video, and relies on free-form data collection that does not guarantee coverage of diverse contextual factors.
eOJ0a5YRoZ.method: RobotEQ-Video has 2K+ videos, 100K+ human annotations, and 17K+ labels for action appropriateness, organized by a four-level coarse-to-fine taxonomy of 6 domains, 20 dimensions, 142 level-1 attributes, and 816 level-2 attributes. The authors also explore how world models can help with the task.
eOJ0a5YRoZ.key_idea: Ground benchmark coverage in a four-level world-state taxonomy (6 domains down to 816 attributes) rather than free-form data collection.
eOJ0a5YRoZ.evidence: Benchmark evaluation of current systems (models unnamed in the abstract) and an exploration of world models.
eOJ0a5YRoZ.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract says current systems still fall short of human performance, with no scores.

ZXrmWhGH1z.one_liner: Agent synthesizes spatial programs progressively for city-scale open-vocabulary 3D grounding, with reversible certification of early exclusions.
ZXrmWhGH1z.problem: In city-scale grounding, the right search scope and geometric computation become clear only as contextual references and local geometry are resolved, and premature filtering can exclude the target.
ZXrmWhGH1z.method: From a query-guided open-vocabulary entity memory, progressive scene-program co-planning adapts search scope and subproblem order, and scene-conditioned geo-code synthesis composes point-cloud and geographic primitives into computations that return execution evidence. Reversible grounding certification checks query requirements and competing hypotheses, directs evidence revision, and tracks dependencies to restore affected alternatives while reusing valid computations.
ZXrmWhGH1z.key_idea: Let search scope and geometric code evolve together with execution evidence, and track dependencies so wrongly excluded candidates can be restored without recomputing valid steps.
ZXrmWhGH1z.evidence: Experiments on CityRefer, CityAnchor, and CitySTAR-3D.
ZXrmWhGH1z.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract only claims effective target disambiguation among visually similar objects and complex spatial relations.

1Ijpq0Nino.one_liner: Builds a downstream classifier from a frozen model's response space in one forward pass using covariance-aware Bayesian Discriminant Mapping.
1Ijpq0Nino.problem: Visual reprogramming optimizes visual prompts through the full frozen model for hundreds of epochs, which remains computationally expensive.
1Ijpq0Nino.method: YORO derives a covariance-aware affine mapping (Bayesian Discriminant Mapping, BDM) from streaming class statistics in one forward-only traversal, with no backpropagation or optimizer updates, and extends to CLIP by treating attribute-prompt similarities as source responses. YORO-FP optionally refines the visual prompt for 20 epochs.
1Ijpq0Nino.key_idea: Fit a covariance-aware affine mapping from streaming class statistics of the frozen model's full response vector, replacing prompt optimization with a single forward-only pass.
1Ijpq0Nino.evidence: Three full-data settings and 16-shot CLIP with four backbones, compared with prior gradient-free mappings.
1Ijpq0Nino.claimed_gains: Average accuracy improves by 18.4--29.2% over the strongest prior gradient-free mapping across three full-data settings, and the four-backbone 16-shot CLIP average rises from 71.4% to 77.2%.

MSbtARE3Xf.one_liner: Preserves a hierarchical response (per-historical-class probabilities, summed new-class probability) with KL-constrained updates for continual graph-text learning.
MSbtARE3Xf.problem: In cross-graph class-incremental learning with graph-text models, new classes can overturn historical predictions even when distinctions among historical classes are preserved, while overly strict response preservation stalls learning of new classes.
MSbtARE3Xf.method: HiRP defines a hierarchical response that keeps each historical-class probability and sums new-class probabilities, preserving historical distinctions and aggregate competition while letting distinctions within the new-class group adapt. The geometry induced by this response guides constrained updates that retain useful adaptation directions and limit response drift.
MSbtARE3Xf.key_idea: Constrain updates to keep each historical-class probability and the summed new-class probability stable, leaving within-new-class distinctions free to change.
MSbtARE3Xf.evidence: Three class-incremental settings with graph-text models, compared with the strongest baseline in each setting.
MSbtARE3Xf.claimed_gains: Absolute gains of 1.84–7.95 percentage points in average accuracy over the strongest compared baseline in each setting, while mitigating zero-shot transfer degradation.

xGSorMAy9Y.one_liner: Estimates 6-DoF pose of unseen objects under hand occlusion by constraining orientation and contact with a few example grasps.
xGSorMAy9Y.problem: Hands obscure parts of an object during interaction, making different poses look alike in egocentric images and degrading object pose estimation for XR.
xGSorMAy9Y.method: HIROP uses a few examples of how an object is held to constrain, at inference, how the object can be oriented relative to the observed hand and where the two should contact. These constraints are combined with visual information to separate visually ambiguous poses, without retraining the underlying model.
xGSorMAy9Y.key_idea: Combine visual pose evidence with grasp priors from a few example holds that constrain object orientation relative to the hand and the hand-object contact location.
xGSorMAy9Y.evidence: Hand interaction datasets including HOT3D-Aria, using eight representative grasps per object and hand side, against visual and hand-object interaction baselines.
xGSorMAy9Y.claimed_gains: On HOT3D-Aria under hand occlusion, ADD-0.1d accuracy improves by 10.3 percentage points over the strongest compared baseline.

LP0sTX3HVt.one_liner: Certifies that no exchange beats a returned subset beyond a tolerance, using one-sided curvature corrections to local data-selection scores.
LP0sTX3HVt.problem: Data-selection scores use local derivatives at a reference model while subset quality is set by retraining, and symmetric uniform approximation bounds also pay for overestimated gains that do not threaten an upper bound.
LP0sTX3HVt.method: Each exchange is modeled as a continuous weight transfer whose local prediction is the starting slope of the retrained-utility curve; under verifiable smoothness and curvature conditions they derive a one-sided correction controlling training-curvature variation and curvature differences between exchanged examples. Combined with scores recomputed at the returned subset's trained model, it covers the whole exchange neighbourhood in one computation without retraining or enumerating alternatives.
LP0sTX3HVt.key_idea: Model each swap as continuous weight transfer and add a one-sided curvature correction that bounds only underestimated retraining gains, so one computation certifies a whole exchange neighbourhood.
LP0sTX3HVt.evidence: Exhaustive CIFAR-10 one-swap auditing of fixed-feature heads, plus a separate endpoint certificate on a fixed empirical detection target (abstract truncated).
LP0sTX3HVt.claimed_gains: On CIFAR-10 one-swap auditing, local prediction overpredicts the maximum retrained gain by 14.3% and the analytic correction adds 0.011% to that prediction while still certifying; a separate endpoint certificate covers four exchanges (rest truncated).

vhs5dmFQ5t.one_liner: Adaptive time-series data selection that estimates pattern-level hardness from loss trajectories over prototype groups and samples instances accordingly.
vhs5dmFQ5t.problem: Conventional training gives all time-series instances equal opportunity, and scoring instances individually ignores the learning state of the temporal patterns they share.
vhs5dmFQ5t.method: PHaSe groups instances into representative pattern groups (prototypes), estimates each group's hardness from recent loss trajectories, transfers it to instance priorities modulated by assignment concentration, and converts them into sampling probabilities. Prototypes are refit on selected instances and merged with historical centers by normalized momentum updates.
vhs5dmFQ5t.key_idea: Rank pattern groups by loss-trajectory hardness, pass that hardness down to instances scaled by assignment concentration, and sample accordingly while prototypes update by momentum.
vhs5dmFQ5t.evidence: Time-series long-term and short-term forecasting and classification, compared with evaluated baselines in individual settings; datasets are unnamed in the abstract.
vhs5dmFQ5t.claimed_gains: Up to 16.4% lower long-term MSE, 4.8% lower short-term sMAPE, and 74.2% higher classification accuracy than evaluated baselines in individual settings, using only half of the training instances per epoch.

rqN2YVfjKz.one_liner: Continual learning for implicit LiDAR localization using temporally validated pseudo poses, frozen readout head, and selective replay.
rqN2YVfjKz.problem: Implicit LiDAR localizers go stale as environments change, and continual updates lack supervision where the historical model fails while unconstrained adaptation can overwrite a still-valid coordinate readout.
rqN2YVfjKz.method: TCPP cross-validates retrieval and scene-coordinate evidence over time to recover pseudo poses for changed or unseen frames; HDER freezes the readout and adapts selected encoder blocks when old scans are inaccessible; MCR reinstates old-scene constraints from historical memory; RAER selects replay as route coverage expands.
rqN2YVfjKz.key_idea: Use the historical localizer both to find changed regions (via pseudo-labels cross-validated over time) and to preserve metric readout (by freezing the head while adapting encoder blocks).
rqN2YVfjKz.claimed_gains: On NCLT, pseudo labels for about 20% of revisit frames suffice for maintenance; the remaining results are truncated.

uciNS2IcSm.one_liner: Hierarchical LiDAR relocalization that routes by spatial context and matches frames in a shared spectral basis, with no routing-specific training.
uciNS2IcSm.problem: Exhaustive frame retrieval costs grow with the map and expose matching to distant aliases, while hierarchical retrieval can discard the correct location during routing because of alias, granularity, and cross-stage embedding mismatches.
uciNS2IcSm.method: Query context routes to spatially coherent map regions, after which the current frame localizes among the retained frames; shared-basis spectral calibration of frame descriptors before aggregation lets regional routing and final matching use the same frame-level similarity.
uciNS2IcSm.key_idea: Calibrate frame descriptors in a shared spectral basis before aggregation so coarse region routing and fine frame matching compare evidence at the same granularity with one similarity.
uciNS2IcSm.evidence: Oxford, NCLT, and MCD, against same-encoder exhaustive retrieval under the original evaluation protocol.
uciNS2IcSm.claimed_gains: Discards 96.1–99.5% of map frames, cuts mean translation error by 54–56% on Oxford and 31–52% on NCLT and MCD, and reduces search time relative to same-encoder exhaustive retrieval.

8HW0yjVoyG.one_liner: Closed-loop UAV active reconstruction from panoramas, using a spherical-ray-adapted VGGT-Omega depth model and scale-adaptive planner initialization.
8HW0yjVoyG.problem: Perspective-based UAV scanning methods need frequent camera adjustments because of their limited field of view.
8HW0yjVoyG.method: FAR is a closed-loop perception-planning-capture framework: a Spherical Ray Adapter (SRA) injects synchronized camera poses into perspective-based VGGT-Omega for streaming metric panoramic depth with cross-window consistency, and Adaptive Initialization sets planning parameters from scene scale. The authors also build a panoramic simulation platform and a large-scale benchmark.
8HW0yjVoyG.key_idea: Exploit omnidirectional observations by adding camera poses to a perspective depth model via a Spherical Ray Adapter, and set planner parameters automatically from scene scale.
8HW0yjVoyG.evidence: Experiments on a new panoramic simulator and benchmark with accurate poses and ground-truth geometry, compared with existing planning and reconstruction methods including MAGICIAN.
8HW0yjVoyG.claimed_gains: With RGB panoramas only, 83.3% coverage with a 1017 m mean path, versus MAGICIAN with ground-truth depth at 79.4% and 1400 m.

oUgyEOMOLU.one_liner: Mid-training distillation that uses teacher predictive entropy to distill on confident tokens and fall back to cross-entropy elsewhere.
oUgyEOMOLU.problem: Forward-KL distillation from post-trained teachers improves reasoning and factual recall in pre-training but slows factual recall acquisition in mid-training, because teachers are more confident on procedural than knowledge-intensive data while students learn low-entropy facts early.
oUgyEOMOLU.method: Switch Distillation distills on tokens where the teacher is confident, using teacher predictive entropy as a lightweight routing signal, and otherwise falls back to cross-entropy.
oUgyEOMOLU.key_idea: Route each token by teacher predictive entropy: distill where the teacher is confident, otherwise train with plain cross-entropy.
oUgyEOMOLU.evidence: Controlled experiments comparing forward-KL distillation with next-token prediction across pre-training and mid-training, and Switch Distillation against existing distillation objectives (abstract truncated).
oUgyEOMOLU.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract only says Switch Distillation consistently outperforms existing distillation objectives.

fosUqOEhwI.one_liner: Unified analysis of Softmax-family losses covering consistency, gradients, convergence bounds, and approximation bias-variance trade-offs.
fosUqOEhwI.problem: Softmax cross-entropy and its scalable approximations lack a unified comparison of their statistical, optimization, and computational properties.
fosUqOEhwI.method: Combines the Fenchel-Young view of softmax with large-class approximation methods. It examines consistency with classification and ranking metrics, gradient structure, score-space smoothness, and a loss-level bias-variance decomposition of approximate methods.
fosUqOEhwI.key_idea: Compare exact and approximate softmax losses through Fenchel-Young consistency, regularized fixed-feature convergence bounds, and a loss-level bias-variance decomposition.
fosUqOEhwI.evidence: Theoretical analysis of consistency, gradients, convergence bounds, and per-epoch computational cost, plus experiments across representative recommendation backbones.

X5VRZwhoQy.one_liner: Quantifies optimal linear regret-transfer constants and gain identities between ranking metrics to explain metric mismatch.
X5VRZwhoQy.problem: Surrogate-loss consistency does not guarantee that different ranking metrics improve together, leaving metric mismatch poorly understood.
X5VRZwhoQy.method: A theoretical framework characterizes optimal linear regret-transfer constants between ranking metrics for fixed binary-relevance lists, derives exact metric-gain identities from cumulative relevance across ranking prefixes, and analyzes score-margin dynamics under binary cross-entropy gradient flow.
X5VRZwhoQy.key_idea: Quantify cross-metric relationships via optimal linear regret-transfer constants and exact gain identities over cumulative relevance across ranking prefixes.
X5VRZwhoQy.evidence: Proofs that global regret transfer and local gain sensitivity can scale differently, and that equal-weight population binary cross-entropy gradient flow with independent logits adds no new relevance-order inversions; no experiments are visible in the abstract.

Fd1h1qnWeE.one_liner: Lightweight Allocator predicts per-frame resolution from query and preview features, trained by cost-aware policy optimization as a contextual bandit.
Fd1h1qnWeE.problem: MLLMs encode video frames at uniform resolution, forcing a rigid trade-off between spatial detail and temporal sampling density under token budgets.
Fd1h1qnWeE.method: A lightweight Allocator pairs coarse preview features with the user query to predict continuous per-frame scales before visual feature extraction, coarsening redundant intervals and giving denser tokens to answer-critical moments. It is trained with Cost-Aware Policy Optimization (CAPO), treating allocation as a continuous-action contextual bandit.
Fd1h1qnWeE.key_idea: Choose per-frame resolution before encoding with a query-conditioned policy trained by CAPO: group-relative advantage with asymmetric cost shaping, temporal-similarity regularization, and concentration penalties.
Fd1h1qnWeE.evidence: Evaluated across diverse video benchmarks, including Qwen2.5-VL at 128 frames on a six-benchmark average.
Fd1h1qnWeE.claimed_gains: On Qwen2.5-VL at 128 frames it matches dense full-resolution accuracy on the six-benchmark average (56.28 vs. 55.85) using only 22.9% of the tokens (abstract truncated after this).

33IggCfKIA.one_liner: Models static scenes with a shared 3D field and distractors with per-image 2D pixel-space fields, separated by asymmetric representation.
33IggCfKIA.problem: Transient objects and their shadows violate NeRF's multi-view consistency assumption, causing floaters and ghosting, and existing distractor separation depends on semantic priors or heuristic rules.
33IggCfKIA.method: Represents the static scene with a shared 3D field and each image's distractors with a per-image 2D field defined in pixel coordinates. An initialization favoring the static branch plus joint optimization drives separation from the first iteration.
33IggCfKIA.key_idea: Exploit cross-view inconsistency of distractors as an inductive bias by pairing a shared 3D static field with per-image 2D pixel-coordinate distractor fields.
33IggCfKIA.evidence: The provided abstract describes the design but no experiments, datasets, or baselines.

iWSoBuMm8J.one_liner: Binds visual source motion tracks to stereo audio generation through motion binding, a spatial track encoder, and residual track RoPE.
iWSoBuMm8J.problem: Joint video-audio generators align semantics and timing but largely ignore stereo audio, whose perceived sound location should follow the motion of its visual source.
iWSoBuMm8J.method: StereoBind uses motion tracks with three mechanisms: Visual Motion Binding for source-aware audiovisual correspondence, a Spatial Track Encoder for absolute source positions, and Residual Track RoPE for relative motion. The authors also build StereoWorld-29K, a stereo audio-video dataset with paired motion tracks, and StereoWorldBench for audiovisual spatial consistency.
iWSoBuMm8J.key_idea: Condition stereo audio generation on visual motion tracks, encoding absolute source position with a track encoder and relative motion with residual track RoPE.
iWSoBuMm8J.evidence: Experiments with the new StereoWorld-29K dataset and StereoWorldBench compare spatial alignment and overall audiovisual quality against existing models.
iWSoBuMm8J.claimed_gains: not stated (qualitative claim only: substantially improved spatial alignment over existing models while preserving overall audiovisual quality)

X79W6F9nPJ.one_liner: Multi-source domain adaptation for conditional diffusion models via weighted empirical risk, used to build a conditional independence test.
X79W6F9nPJ.problem: Generative-model-based conditional independence tests accumulate conditional-distribution estimation error in Type I error bounds, and estimator consistency alone does not guarantee asymptotic Type I error control.
X79W6F9nPJ.method: DA-Diff treats conditional generative modeling as multi-source domain adaptation, training a conditional diffusion model by weighted empirical risk minimization over target and source domains. DA-CIT builds a conditional independence test on top of DA-Diff.
X79W6F9nPJ.key_idea: Weighted empirical risk minimization over target and multiple source domains enlarges effective sample size for the conditional diffusion model while controlling transfer bias.
X79W6F9nPJ.evidence: Proves a convergence rate for DA-Diff and a Type I error guarantee P(p <= alpha) <= alpha + o(1) for DA-CIT; experiments compare conditional generation quality with transfer-learning diffusion baselines (rest of abstract truncated).

aJkD1IYv9x.one_liner: C3D evaluates semantic correspondence by lifting sampled queries and matches to 3D and measuring distortion of normalized intra-object distances.
aJkD1IYv9x.problem: Semantic correspondence is scored only at sparse annotated landmarks (e.g., PCK), leaving predictions between landmarks and the spatial generality of the correspondence field unmeasured.
aJkD1IYv9x.method: C3D probes a fixed correspondence map at independently sampled foreground locations, lifts queries and predicted matches into 3D with monocular point maps, and measures distortion of normalized intra-object distances, either among the samples (annotation-free) or against annotated anchors (annotation-assisted). The annotation-assisted structural residual is also used as supervision to train K2D from pseudo-correspondences obtained by fused semantic-structural transport.
aJkD1IYv9x.key_idea: Score a correspondence field by how much it distorts normalized intra-object 3D distances, with 3D obtained from monocular point maps.
aJkD1IYv9x.evidence: Computed on SPair-71k and compared with SPair-71k PCK as a predictor of method ranking on the unseen keypoints of SPair-U.

nieoP8KEVJ.one_liner: RL for social understanding that builds and validates evidence tests comparing rollout answers, avoiding ground-truth annotation rewards.
nieoP8KEVJ.problem: Social intelligence training depends on human annotation, and social predictions lack verification oracles and are ambiguous because one behavior supports several interpretations.
nieoP8KEVJ.method: Given distinct answers in a rollout group, RLCE constructs evidence tests that identify observable evidence favoring one answer over another, validates them against the input sample, and aggregates outcomes to pick the best-supported interpretation. Tests are regenerated as the policy's answers change during training.
nieoP8KEVJ.key_idea: Derive rewards from validated evidence tests that contrast rollout answers, and regenerate those tests as the policy's answers evolve.
nieoP8KEVJ.evidence: Evaluated on four benchmarks spanning affect, pragmatics, communicative intent, and preference.
nieoP8KEVJ.claimed_gains: not stated (abstract is cut off at 'attains the strongest performance among')

tPmq5mij28.one_liner: Normalizes Gaussian-center spacing instead of radial distance so feed-forward 3DGS predicts consistent Gaussian scales across scene scales.
tPmq5mij28.problem: Feed-forward 3DGS normalizes Gaussian attributes by radial distance, but neighbor spacing still varies with scene scale and camera setup, shifting Gaussian-scale targets and making supervision ambiguous.
tPmq5mij28.method: SplatAnything adds Gaussian Spacing Normalization (GSNorm), which canonicalizes a robust scene-level statistic of Gaussian spacing as the spatial reference for Gaussian prediction. The authors also build a benchmark across diverse datasets, input sparsity levels, and extrapolated viewpoints.
tPmq5mij28.key_idea: Canonicalize a robust scene-level statistic of spacing between neighboring Gaussian centers, replacing radial-distance normalization, to remove ambiguity in Gaussian-scale targets.
tPmq5mij28.evidence: Experiments on a new benchmark spanning diverse datasets, input sparsity levels, and extrapolated viewpoints.
tPmq5mij28.claimed_gains: not stated (qualitative claim only: strong gains under substantial variation in scene scale and viewpoint)

F960FwEmqn.one_liner: Proves transformer masked diffusion models learn mixtures of hidden Markov trees with sample complexity governed by latent structure.
F960FwEmqn.problem: Statistical bounds for masked diffusion models treat parallelization and estimation errors separately and scale with V^L, the number of length-L sequences, suffering the curse of dimensionality.
F960FwEmqn.method: Models latent structure as mixtures of hidden Markov trees and proves end-to-end guarantees for a transformer-based MDM with parallel unmasking schedules. The network and sampler need no knowledge of tree topologies or component parameters.
F960FwEmqn.key_idea: Analyze parallel-unmasking transformer MDMs jointly for parallelization and estimation error under a mixture-of-hidden-Markov-trees assumption, yielding sample complexity that depends on latent structure.
F960FwEmqn.evidence: Theoretical result: epsilon-accurate sampling in KL divergence with O-tilde(L K_par / epsilon) training samples, where K_par is polynomial in L, V, the number of hidden states, and the number of mixture components.
F960FwEmqn.claimed_gains: Theoretical sample complexity of O-tilde(L K_par / epsilon) for epsilon-accurate KL sampling, in place of bounds that scale with V^L; no empirical numbers.

Qad1mUrExr.one_liner: AI scientist that converts Alzheimer's knowledge gaps into feasibility-screened, Elo-ranked hypotheses tested with two-level auditing.
Qad1mUrExr.problem: Automated experimentation does not by itself advance scientific understanding; research agents must find meaningful knowledge gaps, decide what data can resolve them, and judge whether findings add to existing knowledge.
Qad1mUrExr.method: DeepQuest turns unresolved questions from domain reviews into traceable hypotheses, prioritizes them by data feasibility screening and groupwise Elo ranking, and runs iterative experiments. A two-level audit separates experimental reliability from knowledge contribution relative to two frozen literature corpora.
Qad1mUrExr.key_idea: Drive agent research from literature knowledge gaps, ranking hypotheses by data feasibility and Elo, and audit both experimental reliability and contribution against frozen corpora.
Qad1mUrExr.evidence: Tested on OASIS-3 with three language-model reviewers against general-purpose executors and domain-specific research agents, with key associations checked in independent ADNI and AIBL cohorts.
Qad1mUrExr.claimed_gains: On OASIS-3 it produces 42 feasible hypotheses, outperforms the strongest baselines in 14 of 15 evaluator-dimension comparisons, and reaches an audit-assessed scientific finding rate of 95.24%.

8mD5ZUCb6Q.one_liner: Benchmark of 300 tasks testing interactive world models over 60-180 second rollouts for sustained control and revisit memory.
8mD5ZUCb6Q.problem: Short-term visual quality and action following give limited evidence that an interactive world model stays reliable during extended use.
8mD5ZUCb6Q.method: Two task suites (sustained control; revisit memory with six trajectory families of delayed and repeated revisits) with 60-180 second target rollouts. Scoring combines automatic visual and motion measurements with scene-specific checklists for visual quality, temporal consistency, revisit retention, physical and causal validity, and camera responses.
8mD5ZUCb6Q.key_idea: Evaluate long-horizon world models with revisit-memory trajectories and scene-tailored checklists in addition to automatic visual and motion measurements.
8mD5ZUCb6Q.evidence: Evaluates 12 interactive world models on the 300-task benchmark.

nS97QKfsvR.one_liner: Jointly trains video diffusion with teacher forcing and bidirectional attention (MoBA) for causal pre-training of autoregressive world models.
nS97QKfsvR.problem: Adapting pretrained bidirectional video diffusion models into autoregressive ones with teacher forcing disrupts visual priors and degrades autoregressive generation quality.
nS97QKfsvR.method: Mix Forcing trains with Mixture-of-Bidirectional-and-Autoregressive (MoBA) attention: teacher forcing learns causal next-chunk prediction while bidirectional attention preserves pretrained visual priors, and chunk-wise cross-attention conditions each chunk on a shared environment prompt and its own local prompt. After causal pre-training on a 14B image-to-video model, consistency and distribution matching distillation give a four-step autoregressive generator.
nS97QKfsvR.key_idea: Mix teacher-forced causal attention and bidirectional attention in one self-attention (MoBA) during pre-training so the causal initialization keeps the pretrained visual priors.
nS97QKfsvR.evidence: Experiments on an internal benchmark and public benchmarks including WBench and SANA-WM-Bench, using a causally pre-trained 14B image-to-video model.
nS97QKfsvR.claimed_gains: not stated (abstract is cut off at 'achieves state-of-the-art visual quality')

RwlE7cce7R.one_liner: Replaces attention with an input-dependent global convolution, causal along time and circular across variables, for high-dimensional forecasting.
RwlE7cce7R.problem: Variable-wise attention costs quadratic time in the number of variables, and fast global convolution wraps the end of an axis to its start, which leaks targets along the time axis.
RwlE7cce7R.method: Time Fluxer (TiF) uses a fast input-dependent global convolution (the fluxer) in place of attention, with causal closure along time and circular closure across variables, so every position is trained to forecast what follows it.
RwlE7cce7R.key_idea: Give the two axes different convolution closures: causal along time to avoid target leakage, circular across variables because they have no first or last element.
RwlE7cce7R.evidence: Seven Time-HD datasets, swapping the fluxer in for iTransformer's variable-wise attention and PatchTST's patch-wise attention, plus comparing one causally trained model against models trained separately per history length.
RwlE7cce7R.claimed_gains: Replacing variable-wise attention (iTransformer) with the fluxer reduces error in 26 of 28 settings and replacing patch-wise attention (PatchTST) in 21 of 28; one causally trained model beats separately trained models in 26 of 35 dataset-history comparisons.

ir6D54QOU0.one_liner: Explores all best-of-N video candidates under training-free feature caching, then regenerates only the winner at full compute.
ir6D54QOU0.problem: Test-time search for video diffusion fully denoises every candidate although only the verifier's ranking of the discarded candidates is used, which wastes compute.
ir6D54QOU0.method: CachedSearch scores all candidates with aggressive training-free feature caching, picks the verifier's winner, and regenerates only that winner from its seed at full compute, so the returned sample is always an exact full-compute sample.
ir6D54QOU0.key_idea: Use cheap cached rollouts only to preserve the verifier's candidate ranking, then regenerate the top-ranked seed at full compute.
ir6D54QOU0.evidence: 7,552 seed-matched cached and full-compute Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B videos on VBench, plus a Gaussian-copula model relating preserved search gain to rank correlation.
ir6D54QOU0.claimed_gains: Caching that halves candidate cost gives a median per-prompt Spearman correlation of 0.905 with zero median regret; at N = 8 it retains 94% of best-of-8's reward gain at 63% of its cost, and for under 2% more cost than best-of-4 it searches six candidates for 11% more gain, with pruning exploring candidates 3.12x more cheaply.

WDQ8DZUqyJ.one_liner: Selects diffusion-codec noise atoms for any differentiable objective by finding an optimal linear function, one VJP per guided step.
WDQ8DZUqyJ.problem: Zero-shot diffusion codecs such as Turbo-DDCM only control the latent-space quadratic objective, and no scalable method optimizes compression for arbitrary loss functions.
WDQ8DZUqyJ.method: LOONA determines the optimal linear function for a given differentiable objective to choose noise atoms, so cost does not scale with codebook size K. Each guided step computes one vector-Jacobian product, and it keeps Turbo-DDCM's bitstream format and frozen decoder with no side information or retraining.
WDQ8DZUqyJ.key_idea: Linearize an arbitrary differentiable objective over noise atoms so selection needs a single vector-Jacobian product instead of evaluating candidate combinations.
WDQ8DZUqyJ.evidence: Experiments with pixel-level fidelity, semantic preservation, and perceptual objectives show LOONA optimizes the given objectives; remaining results are cut off in the abstract.

4cKnr4IZtH.one_liner: Training-free T2I steering via a closed-form nonlinear orthogonal attribute space built from exemplars, with interventions in latent space.
4cKnr4IZtH.problem: T2I diffusion models give biased outputs from entangled priors; prompt and embedding interventions are imprecise and adversarially vulnerable, fine-tuning is invasive, and text cannot control evaluative attributes.
4cKnr4IZtH.method: LatentCompass builds a nonlinear, low-dimensional, orthogonal attribute space from exemplars with a closed-form solution, defines a target-class intervention in that space, and reflects it in the T2I latent space to steer the generative trajectory without training.
4cKnr4IZtH.key_idea: Isolate concepts in a closed-form orthogonal attribute space, intervene on the target class there, and map the intervention back into the diffusion latent space.
4cKnr4IZtH.evidence: Evaluations on debiasing medical professions, unsafe concept generation, aesthetic score, red-teaming against Deepfake detectors, and attribute editing.
4cKnr4IZtH.claimed_gains: On average it mitigates generative stereotypes in medical professions by 100%, reduces unsafe concept generation to 1.3%, enhances aesthetic score by 27%, and boosts red-teaming success against Deepfake detectors by 40%.

8sauzhDFWg.one_liner: High-probability convergence upper and lower bounds for standard nonconvex SGD under heavy-tailed noise with bounded alpha-th central moment.
8sauzhDFWg.problem: It was unresolved whether standard SGD converges for L-smooth nonconvex objectives when gradient noise has only a bounded alpha-th central moment with 1 < alpha < 2.
8sauzhDFWg.method: They prove a high-probability bound for SGD with a confidence-calibrated learning rate and a high-probability lower bound for any deterministic learning-rate schedule with step size at most 1/L.
8sauzhDFWg.key_idea: Set the learning rate from the confidence level delta for a high-probability rate, and prove a lower bound with delta^(-1/alpha) dependence for any deterministic schedule.
8sauzhDFWg.evidence: Theoretical proofs only: an upper bound holding with probability at least 1-delta and a lower bound in the nontrivial regime that matches the joint L and sigma dependence when sigma^2 is of order L*Delta.
8sauzhDFWg.claimed_gains: Average squared gradient norm is O(L*Delta/T + sigma*sqrt(L*Delta)/(delta^(1/alpha) T^((alpha-1)/alpha))) with probability at least 1-delta, with a lower bound of order min{L*Delta, sigma^2}/(delta^(1/alpha) T^((alpha-1)/alpha)).

oGXyvI1PX8.one_liner: Feed-forward network registers mesh sequences by querying a global motion embedding with topology-aware anchor-mesh point features.
oGXyvI1PX8.problem: Existing non-rigid registration models depend on costly per-instance optimization, narrow object categories, pairwise-only inputs, or only produce intermediate outputs.
oGXyvI1PX8.method: A topology-aware point representation encodes the anchor mesh's topology into per-vertex features, and a multi-modal encoder fuses it with per-frame shape latents and image features into a compact global motion embedding. A lightweight decoder queries this embedding with the anchor-mesh point features to retrieve per-vertex deformations at target timestamps.
oGXyvI1PX8.key_idea: Encode a mesh sequence into one global motion embedding, then decode per-vertex deformations by querying it with anchor-mesh features that carry topology (separating geodesically distant points).
oGXyvI1PX8.evidence: Extensive experiments across diverse motions and object categories on non-rigid registration, including a runtime comparison against the fastest baseline.
oGXyvI1PX8.claimed_gains: Reduces CD-Motion by up to 28% while running nearly twice as fast as the fastest baseline.

zOJtjt0U3B.one_liner: Re-ranks retrieved Cell Ontology candidates with a differentiable fuzzy description-logic reasoner for ontology-consistent cell type annotation.
zOJtjt0U3B.problem: Single-cell foundation models treat annotation as flat classification and violate Cell Ontology axioms, with one in five to seven predictions breaking a hard biological law.
zOJtjt0U3B.method: FuzzyCell retrieves candidate cell types with a pretrained encoder and re-ranks them with a differentiable fuzzy description logic reasoner. Training uses the sigmoidal Reichenbach implication, for which they prove the ontology loss reweights each axiom evaluation by a logistic function of its own truth value.
zOJtjt0U3B.key_idea: Frame annotation as ontology-constrained entity linking, training with a sigmoidal Reichenbach fuzzy implication loss that damps vacuously satisfied axiom evaluations.
zOJtjt0U3B.evidence: An audit of scGPT, Geneformer, CellFM, and scCello on Tabula Sapiens, and evaluation on Tabula Sapiens, HLCA, and AIDA v2 against the 65,000+ logical axioms of the Cell Ontology.
zOJtjt0U3B.claimed_gains: Cuts axiom violations by over 80% and lifts Macro-F1 by 4 to 8 points over the respective backbone on Tabula Sapiens, HLCA, and AIDA v2.

UJP9R8H85G.one_liner: Recursively self-improves a shared navigation model by generating instructions for unlabeled trajectories in small shards and filtering by execution outcome.
UJP9R8H85G.problem: Vision-language navigation needs high-quality language supervision, but existing synthesis methods use separate models or task-specific coupling and annotate the whole corpus with a fixed model, so supervision lags behind the evolving policy.
UJP9R8H85G.method: RSI-Nav unifies instruction following and instruction generation in one shared model, then after SFT processes unlabeled trajectories in small shards: the current model writes instructions, executes them to score goal completion and path efficiency, and the retained samples update the policy. Spatial understanding data is also added.
UJP9R8H85G.key_idea: Policy-synchronized dual bootstrapping: the current model generates instructions for each shard, executes them to filter samples, and updates before annotating the next shard.
UJP9R8H85G.evidence: not stated; the abstract is cut off before the experiments.

3OKkj4tdg3.one_liner: Asynchronous mixture of transformers refreshes a structured interaction state only when needed, with cached key-value features guiding an action expert.
3OKkj4tdg3.problem: Manipulation policies couple interaction reasoning to control frequency or predefined task structure, mismatching when robots act with when they need to reason.
3OKkj4tdg3.method: Given a task instruction, AsyncMoT maintains a structured interaction state (stage, target object, action-relevant region) and selectively refreshes it; between updates cached key-value features carry guidance while the action expert adapts motor commands to current observations. The decoupling lets interaction supervision be shared across robot tasks and human videos without action correspondence.
3OKkj4tdg3.key_idea: Make when to reason an explicit policy decision: refresh a structured interaction state only at interaction-dependent moments and reuse cached key-value features between refreshes.
3OKkj4tdg3.evidence: Evaluations on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, RoboCasa-24, and RoboCasa365, covering long-horizon, distribution-shifted, and compositional manipulation.
3OKkj4tdg3.claimed_gains: Average success rates of 98.1% on LIBERO, 88.9% on LIBERO-Plus, 66.3% on RoboCasa-24, and 35.9% on RoboCasa365.

1aJwsAZFZJ.one_liner: One [SEG] token is decomposed into instance-aware queries and verified by spatial evidence for generalized referring segmentation.
1aJwsAZFZJ.problem: In generalized referring segmentation an expression may match zero, one, or many instances; MLLM methods emitting multiple [SEG] tokens risk missing or duplicated tokens, while mask-query methods underuse autoregressive reasoning.
1aJwsAZFZJ.method: OneSEG uses a single [SEG] token for the shared referential semantics; Semantic-to-Instance Query Decomposition (SIQD) turns it into instance-aware queries conditioned on visual evidence, and an Instance Evidence Verifier (IEV) checks decoded candidates with explicit spatial evidence.
1aJwsAZFZJ.key_idea: Capture shared referential semantics in one [SEG] token and defer instance enumeration to the decoder by decomposing it into visual-evidence-conditioned instance queries.
1aJwsAZFZJ.evidence: Experiments on generalized referring segmentation benchmarks (abstract truncated before results).

IssvRu624q.one_liner: Benchmark where models locate a target on an allocentric map from multiple egocentric views, with floor-plan and controlled-triangle subsets.
IssvRu624q.problem: It is unclear whether frontier multimodal models' gains in spatial reasoning reflect robust reasoning or reliance on familiar correspondences between representations.
IssvRu624q.method: REMAP, based on cognitive-science settings, combines FLOORPLAN (indoor layouts) and TRIANGLE, a controlled diagnostic that varies the geometric correspondence between local views and the global map.
IssvRu624q.key_idea: Vary how egocentric views correspond to the allocentric map in a controlled diagnostic to test whether models are robust to correspondence changes, as humans are.
IssvRu624q.evidence: 24 vision-language models and human participants evaluated on FLOORPLAN and TRIANGLE.
IssvRu624q.claimed_gains: Across 24 vision-language models, capability ranges from below random to surpassing average human performance on FLOORPLAN, while simple correspondence changes in TRIANGLE cause significant drops that humans largely avoid.

qLvIIWHL23.one_liner: Turns black-box rewards into reward-tilted marginal velocity fields that serve as evolving distribution-matching-distillation targets for few-step generators.
qLvIIWHL23.problem: Black-box rewards give only scalar scores for final samples and do not specify the target distribution or marginal velocity field that Distribution Matching Distillation requires.
qLvIIWHL23.method: RISE-DMD trains a Reward Score model on on-policy student samples and their reward feedback to learn a reward-improved marginal velocity field, which DMD uses to update the few-step student. The updated student generates data for the next round, so the target distribution evolves with the student.
qLvIIWHL23.key_idea: Learn a Reward Score field from on-policy samples and rewards, use it as the DMD target, and iterate so target and student distributions evolve together.
qLvIIWHL23.evidence: Main experiment on SD3.5 Medium, plus Sana 1.6B, DrawBench, and OCR results, with a theoretical characterization of the population-optimal Reward Score field.
qLvIIWHL23.claimed_gains: On SD3.5 Medium it outperforms the compared methods on all six preference and quality metrics, three of which are not used for training.

dbIhe5K1A8.one_liner: Accelerates four-step autoregressive video diffusion with a lightweight predictor guided by the previous chunk's same-timestep features.
dbIhe5K1A8.problem: Feature caching fails when only four denoising steps remain, because large feature changes between timesteps undermine both direct reuse and lightweight predictors.
dbIhe5K1A8.method: TGuide's Anchor-Transport-Correct (ATC) predictor combines the current chunk's preceding-step features, which preserve spatial structure, with the previous chunk's same-timestep features, using spatial retrieval and adaptive correction. The predictor is trained on its own autoregressive rollouts, and an optional confidence-aware scheduler adjusts the quality-efficiency trade-off.
dbIhe5K1A8.key_idea: Predict velocity by spatially retrieving from the previous chunk's same-timestep features and correcting the current chunk's preceding-step features, trained on the predictor's own rollouts.
dbIhe5K1A8.evidence: Experiments on Self Forcing, Causal Forcing, and HY-WorldPlay (the abstract is cut off before the results).

aDoLDn9LPA.one_liner: End-to-end model jointly generating transcript, speaker identities and timestamps for 90-minute audio, trained with speaker-tag corruption plus RL.
aDoLDn9LPA.problem: In autoregressive transcription of long multi-speaker conversations, incorrect speaker labels in the history influence later predictions and cause persistent attribution errors.
aDoLDn9LPA.method: Speaker Identity-Preserving Optimization (SIPO) combines Speaker Identity Decoupling SFT, which perturbs historical speaker tags and trains corrective attribution while accounting for speaker-ID renaming equivalence, with RL that optimizes complete transcripts using a cpCER and DER reward.
aDoLDn9LPA.key_idea: Train on perturbed speaker-tag histories with renaming-invariant corrective targets, then optimize whole transcripts with RL rewarding cpCER and DER.
aDoLDn9LPA.evidence: AISHELL-4, AliMeeting, Podcast and Movies benchmarks, plus an analysis of 32 internal two-speaker recordings.
aDoLDn9LPA.claimed_gains: Lowest cpCER among the evaluated systems with available results; on AISHELL-4, RL initialized from SID training reaches 15.83% cpCER versus 24.30% for RL initialized without SID.

CHsbZrNf1T.one_liner: Paired benchmark of 8,000 cases that inject mid-task events into LIBERO tasks to measure robot policy robustness.
CHsbZrNf1T.problem: Many simulation robustness benchmarks fix external conditions at reset, leaving unexamined the need to continue a task after a target moves, the viewpoint shifts, or an obstacle appears.
CHsbZrNf1T.method: LIBERO-MAX has 8,000 paired cases across eight change types covering geometry, observations, appearance, clutter, and paths. Each pair compares execution with and without a mid-task event while holding the task, initial state, policy seed, and pre-event actions fixed.
CHsbZrNf1T.key_idea: Pair each rollout with an otherwise identical no-event rollout, so event-associated regressions are separated from failures already present.
CHsbZrNf1T.evidence: Evaluation of fourteen current VLA, hybrid, and world-action policies, with camera controls and varied query cadence.
CHsbZrNf1T.claimed_gains: Across fourteen policies, mid-task events reduce success by 11.0-25.7 percentage points.

lzak3g6k9v.one_liner: Recurrent memory that caches state checkpoints as anchors with content keys, and attends over them at each token.
lzak3g6k9v.problem: Recurrent models compress history into a fixed-size state and underperform on recall-intensive tasks because earlier associations are overwritten, while Transformers pay quadratic training cost and a growing KV cache.
lzak3g6k9v.method: MARCH periodically caches cumulative recurrent-state checkpoints as state anchors, each with a compact content-conditioned anchor key, forming a memory bank that grows with context length. At each token an anchor query attends over the causally available anchors, and the output aggregates historical-anchor readouts with the current-state readout in an attention-style manner.
lzak3g6k9v.key_idea: Store periodic recurrent-state snapshots keyed by content and let each token route over them with attention, trading historical resolution against memory cost.
lzak3g6k9v.evidence: The visible abstract is truncated before any experiments or results are described.

Ee0tmUEUgL.one_liner: Progressively prunes Earth observation foundation models using output-sensitive scoring and representative calibration before downstream fine-tuning.
Ee0tmUEUgL.problem: Adapting and deploying Earth observation foundation models is computationally expensive, and structural importance shifts as the encoder and a new decoder train together while heterogeneous EO data make importance estimates sensitive to calibration inputs.
Ee0tmUEUgL.method: NewOrder performs structured pruning before full downstream fine-tuning, combining output-sensitive scoring, progressive pruning, and representative calibration.
Ee0tmUEUgL.key_idea: Re-estimate structural importance progressively during adaptation, using output-sensitive scores computed on calibration data chosen to represent heterogeneous EO inputs.
Ee0tmUEUgL.evidence: Four encoders and four downstream tasks against other pruning methods, plus full efficiency profiling.
Ee0tmUEUgL.claimed_gains: At 50% compression it is best among compared pruning methods in 14 of 16 settings and exceeds dense adaptation in 8, with up to 1.73x inference speedup, 1.72x training-step speedup, and 33.4% lower peak training memory.

ca93JxlBvH.one_liner: EgoWAM predicts future 3D semantic fields and hand motions, scoring candidate actions with spatial-semantic optimal transport for egocentric interaction.
ca93JxlBvH.problem: World models in image space are perturbed by arbitrary head motion in egocentric hand-object interaction, entangling physical interaction dynamics with viewpoint shifts.
ca93JxlBvH.method: A world action model autoregressively predicts future 3D semantic fields (dense semantic features anchored to scene geometry) and hand motions, with a diffusion-based action head giving a prior for sampling candidate actions. Candidates are scored by an optimal transport objective that aligns semantic features under a 3D transport cost.
ca93JxlBvH.key_idea: Model dynamics in a 3D semantic field anchored to scene geometry to remove viewpoint dependence, and plan by optimal-transport matching of predicted and goal features.
ca93JxlBvH.evidence: Experiments on rigid and articulated egocentric hand-object interaction datasets, evaluating world-state prediction, motion forecasting and goal-directed planning.
ca93JxlBvH.claimed_gains: Improved performance in world-state prediction, motion forecasting and goal-directed planning; no numbers stated.

gncPyBZgyG.one_liner: Systematic study of Mixture-of-Experts design and training for large-scale audio-visual diffusion models, with dense text conditioning and routing regulation.
gncPyBZgyG.problem: Existing MoE design choices may not suit audio-visual latent tokens, which have strong spatial, temporal and cross-modal correlations.
gncPyBZgyG.method: Strengthens text conditioning with richer semantic representations while keeping that branch dense and allocating sparse capacity to the visual backbone. Combines routing regulation with targeted stabilization to preserve normal expert differentiation and suppress instability-driven collapse.
gncPyBZgyG.key_idea: Sparse capacity goes only to the visual backbone, while routing regulation plus targeted stabilization separate semantic expert specialization from instability-driven load collapse.
gncPyBZgyG.evidence: Validated with millions of high-quality audio-visual samples in a large-scale distributed training environment.

aBjJ2aYnWn.one_liner: Post-trains a text-to-two-human interaction generator with physics-decoupled diffusion DPO using preferences from simulated humanoid tracking rollouts.
aBjJ2aYnWn.problem: Limited tracking capability restricts which reference interaction motions can be executed, and successful tracking does not guarantee physically plausible responses or faithful interactions.
aBjJ2aYnWn.method: DIGHT executes multiple text-conditioned interaction candidates in simulation with a fixed tracker, builds physics-grounded preferences for executability (tracking error, friction, floating) and interaction fidelity (simulator force feedback as a contact measure), and aligns the generator with physics-decoupled diffusion DPO without differentiating through the simulator.
aBjJ2aYnWn.key_idea: Separate preference pairs for executability and for contact-force interaction fidelity feed diffusion DPO, keeping criterion-specific supervision without a single scalar reward.
aBjJ2aYnWn.evidence: Simulation rollouts with a fixed humanoid tracker; evaluation details are cut off in the abstract.

vMStDQtxGX.one_liner: Three-system VLA pretraining: an action expert, scene understanding with task decomposition, and a world value model predicting futures and progress.
vMStDQtxGX.problem: Staged VLA training separates vision-language adaptation from continuous-action learning, and world models in VLA pipelines do not couple future-state prediction with task-progress evaluation for long-horizon manipulation.
vMStDQtxGX.method: System 1 turns multimodal context into continuous actions, System 2 handles scene understanding and task decomposition, and System 3 predicts future observations and estimates task progress. A VLM backbone and action expert are trained jointly with understanding objectives, Soft Knowledge Insulation attenuates action gradients into the backbone, and a frozen World Value Model guides post-training.
vMStDQtxGX.key_idea: Train the VLM and action expert jointly with attenuated action gradients into the backbone, and use a frozen model that predicts future observations and task progress to guide post-training.
vMStDQtxGX.evidence: Multi-embodiment VLA pretraining across robot embodiments (per TLDR); experimental details are cut off in the abstract.

zB8mGtaVvc.one_liner: Plug-in GCD regularizer enforcing assignment consistency under low-frequency amplitude mixing and between a stable-token pool and the global descriptor.
zB8mGtaVvc.problem: GCD models may rely on appearance cues such as texture, illumination, and background, which distort feature similarity and make category assignments unstable.
zB8mGtaVvc.method: Image-level Consistency Regularization mixes low-frequency amplitudes across images while keeping the source phase and asks the mixed image to keep the clean image's assignment. Token-level Consistency Regularization pools patch tokens that stay stable after spectral filtering into a Stable Semantic Token and aligns its assignment with the global descriptor.
zB8mGtaVvc.key_idea: Regularize category assignments to be invariant to frequency-domain appearance changes via amplitude mixing at image level and stable-token agreement at token level.
zB8mGtaVvc.evidence: The visible abstract is cut off before the experiments; not stated.

Iv3vw1NRsk.one_liner: Animates avatars interacting with objects in Gaussian Splatting scenes via Gaussian-derived occupancy maps, SDF proxies, and contact refinement.
Iv3vw1NRsk.problem: Animation pipelines rely on meshes or point clouds, which lack photorealism and are hard to recover from casual video, while 3DGS gives photorealism but none of the geometry needed for motion synthesis and contact.
Iv3vw1NRsk.method: Four components operate on opacity-filtered Gaussians: occupancy maps for path planning, an egocentric walkability grid for zero-shot locomotion, a differentiable SDF proxy for interaction synthesis, and differentiable contact refinement for human-scene, human-object, and object-scene contact.
Iv3vw1NRsk.key_idea: Derive occupancy, walkability, SDF, and contact quantities directly from opacity-filtered Gaussians, recomputed as object poses change, so planning and contact need no mesh.
Iv3vw1NRsk.evidence: SuperSplat and DL3DV scenes, with human and VLM preference studies.
Iv3vw1NRsk.claimed_gains: Human and VLM preference studies favour the renderings (abstract truncated); no numbers stated.

oaPOjHKT4s.one_liner: Relational foundation model that retrieves task-relevant records from an evolving external relational memory with reward-guided feedback.
oaPOjHKT4s.problem: Flattening relational databases hides key connections, graph methods add task-irrelevant relational context, and existing pretraining objectives under-use relational information.
oaPOjHKT4s.method: RaMA keeps relational information through a relation-based backbone, retrieves task-relevant records with task-aware queries from a dynamically evolving external relational memory for adaptive fusion with local context, and refines the memory with reward-guided feedback.
oaPOjHKT4s.key_idea: Retrieve task-relevant records from an external relational memory with task-aware queries, and refine that memory through reward-guided feedback.
oaPOjHKT4s.evidence: Empirical experiments motivate the three stated limitations; results for RaMA are cut off in the abstract.

UAFETVqcnu.one_liner: Query-level memory retrieval over an online-clustered KV cache for autoregressive multi-shot video generation.
UAFETVqcnu.problem: Frame-level retrieval with one shared historical context for all query tokens ignores their differing information needs, causing redundant retrieval and inefficient use of memory.
UAFETVqcnu.method: Historical tokens are organized into an online-clustered KV cache guided by attention memory-access patterns, and a query-level retrieval mechanism gives each query broader access to history under a fixed retrieval budget.
UAFETVqcnu.key_idea: Cluster historical KV tokens online into semantic groups and let each query token retrieve its own clusters under a fixed budget.
UAFETVqcnu.evidence: Attention analysis of memory-access patterns motivates the design; experimental results are cut off in the abstract.

TmluMg1fb7.one_liner: Flow-matching video model trained with dual warped noisy anchors and cross-anchor consistency for continuous-viewpoint generation without novel-view RGB supervision.
TmluMg1fb7.problem: Multi-view flow-matching world models are restricted to fixed camera rigs, and continuous camera poses need costly paired pose-video data with dense pose coverage.
TmluMg1fb7.method: For each target pose, source views are geometrically warped into noisy anchors; masked dual-anchor supervision and cross-anchor denoising-output consistency mitigate anchor-specific errors, with a proof under an affine Gaussian surrogate.
TmluMg1fb7.key_idea: Regularize flow-matching outputs from two warped noisy anchors to agree, recovering the clean-reference optimum without ground-truth novel-view RGB.
TmluMg1fb7.evidence: Cosmos-Drive-Dreams and nuScenes autonomous-driving video generation, plus a proof under an affine Gaussian surrogate.
TmluMg1fb7.claimed_gains: On nuScenes, lowest FVD and FVMD among evaluated baselines, reducing FVD by over 31% relative to the best baseline, and best FID and instance preservation with source-conditioned inference.

FePIh2B8Mh.one_liner: Measuring cross-image watermark residual decodability isolates forgery-enabling architectural factors and motivates CoverLock to bind watermarks to cover images.
FePIh2B8Mh.problem: Neural image watermarks can be forged by extracting watermark-bearing residuals from released images and transferring them onto unrelated images, and the causes of this vulnerability remain poorly understood.
FePIh2B8Mh.method: The authors define residual transferability (RT) to quantify cross-image watermark decodability and use controlled interventions to identify two architectural mechanisms that bind watermark evidence to the cover image. For deployed models where redesign is impractical, they propose CoverLock, a plug-and-play defense that strengthens cover-image dependence without architectural changes.
FePIh2B8Mh.key_idea: Quantify cross-image decodability of extracted watermark residuals via residual transferability and suppress forgery by strengthening watermark dependence on the cover image via CoverLock.
FePIh2B8Mh.evidence: Supported by comparative analyses and controlled interventions across high- and low-RT watermarking architectures and evaluations of CoverLock on high-RT watermarking systems.

3m0toOSyx4.one_liner: Mapping live faces onto a compact hyperbolic manifold under liveness-preserving appearance augmentations enables open-set cross-domain face anti-spoofing.
3m0toOSyx4.problem: Symmetric Euclidean classification of live and spoof faces overlooks class asymmetry, struggling to maintain a compact live representation while accommodating diverse spoof attacks across unseen domains.
3m0toOSyx4.method: HypLive-FAS uses Hyperbolic Live-Manifold Learning (HLM) to organize genuine face representations into a compact manifold in hyperbolic space and detect spoofs via deviations into the expanding exterior volume. Liveness-Preserving Augmentation (LPA) perturbs domain-dependent appearance while enforcing consistency to prevent manifold drift across domains.
3m0toOSyx4.key_idea: Concentrate genuine faces onto a compact hyperbolic manifold so diverse spoofs separate into expanding exterior space, stabilized under domain shifts by liveness-preserving appearance augmentations.
3m0toOSyx4.evidence: Evaluated on cross-domain face anti-spoofing against open-ended spoof attacks in unseen domains.

DSNb2D3ccg.one_liner: Unifying continuous and discrete GFlowNet mixtures motivates Doob h-transform stratum-conditioned samplers that partition discrete state spaces for parallel training.
DSNb2D3ccg.problem: Ensembles of GFlowNets improve discrete state-space exploration over single samplers yet add substantial runtime overhead and lack a unifying theoretical framework.
DSNb2D3ccg.method: The paper formulates a theoretical framework covering continuously indexed GFlowNet mixtures—analyzed as random-feature expansions—and discretely indexed mixtures that subsume prior training schemes. Inspired by Doob's h-transform, it introduces Stratum-Conditioned (SC) GFlowNets, which partition the state space via a modular function so each component samples a distinct subset under centralized or embarrassingly parallel training.
DSNb2D3ccg.key_idea: Partition the discrete state space using a prescribed modular function inspired by Doob's h-transform so each GFlowNet mixture component samples a disjoint subset independently.
DSNb2D3ccg.evidence: Supported by expressivity proofs on graph-structured tasks for continuously indexed mixtures and empirical convergence and mode-coverage experiments for Stratum-Conditioned GFlowNets.

jWDgcTT1J7.one_liner: Stress-tests image-editing reward models under Best-of-N search and patches reward blind spots using defect-factor sensitivity profiling.
jWDgcTT1J7.problem: Static human-agreement benchmarks fail to expose reward hacking and defect blind spots when image-editing reward models guide multi-candidate search or iterative refinement.
jWDgcTT1J7.method: EditStress-Bench evaluates image-editing reward models across 300 human-object editing tasks under Best-of-N selection and iterative refinement with human quality and defect annotations. To mitigate search-time failures, factor-guided reward patching profiles a reward model's sensitivity across defect categories and focuses fine-tuning updates on under-detected failure factors.
jWDgcTT1J7.key_idea: Profile an editing reward model's sensitivity to specific visual defect factors under search pressure and target weak factors with focused fine-tuning patches.
jWDgcTT1J7.evidence: Evaluates twelve reward configurations from six families on 300 human-object editing tasks under Best-of-N (up to 64 candidates) and iterative refinement with human quality and defect ratings.
jWDgcTT1J7.claimed_gains: Source-aware rewards remain 10.6 Overall Human Quality (OHQ) points below the human oracle on average at Best-of-64, while factor-guided reward patching improves OHQ by 1.6 to 2.1 points versus 0.3 to 0.4 points for equal-budget random updates.

dUolVvDrTL.one_liner: Compiling tool plans and validating existing answer candidates lets COPA execute tasks with fewer model calls.
dUolVvDrTL.problem: Repeated model calls process growing tool histories, while interface mismatches and omitted candidates prevent single-call plans or answers from succeeding.
dUolVvDrTL.method: COPA uses a compiler to repair resolvable tool-interface mismatches and execute plans from one planning call. An answer processor validates and selects complete candidates already in model responses, with optional model feedback for revision.
dUolVvDrTL.key_idea: Compile model-generated tool plans by repairing interface mismatches, and recover omitted answers by validating complete candidates already present in responses.
dUolVvDrTL.evidence: Shared-tool comparisons use Qwen and Gemma on DeepPlanning's original Shopping tasks, with additional evaluation on AppWorld public train.
dUolVvDrTL.claimed_gains: COPA uses 94.3%–97.2% fewer total model tokens than ReAct and CodeAct on Shopping, and completes 78/90 AppWorld tasks with 81.6% fewer tokens than Simplified ReAct.

skoBAkjFAr.one_liner: Weighting target-relevant poisoned response positions implants diffusion-language-model backdoors through the forward masking process.
skoBAkjFAr.problem: Backdoor vulnerabilities in diffusion language models remain underexplored relative to autoregressive models.
skoBAkjFAr.method: BadDLM trains with a trigger-aware objective that weights target-relevant response positions in poisoned samples. It instantiates concept injection, semantic attribute steering, alignment bypass, and code payload injection targets.
skoBAkjFAr.key_idea: A trigger-aware poisoned-sample objective induces a forward masking distribution that implants backdoors in diffusion language models.
skoBAkjFAr.evidence: Theory establishes equivalence to an induced masking distribution, and experiments on mainstream open-source DLMs evaluate diverse targets, benign utility, and autoregressive-backdoor defenses.

K6xVTbHAb9.one_liner: Scanning learned compact input matrices approximates reusable context blocks' state updates in frozen state-space models.
K6xVTbHAb9.problem: In-place recurrent updates prevent state-space models from reusing repeated context blocks through Transformer-style cache reuse.
K6xVTbHAb9.method: StateBridge learns a compact input matrix for each reusable context block to approximate its state update across preceding contexts. Serving scans this matrix from the live recurrent state instead of prefilling the raw block.
K6xVTbHAb9.key_idea: Replace a repeated context block with a learned compact input matrix whose scan approximates the block's transition from different recurrent states.
K6xVTbHAb9.evidence: Evaluation across four benchmarks measures retained performance and time to first token under context reuse.
K6xVTbHAb9.claimed_gains: StateBridge retains 88.69%–101.07% of performance and achieves up to 2.71× speedup in time to first token across four benchmarks.

aDeomF7brH.one_liner: Replacing a concentrated normalization factor with a deterministic value yields a scalar approximation to dropout's output effect.
aDeomF7brH.problem: It is unclear when normalized dropout outputs admit an accurate common scalar approximation and how much random variation remains.
aDeomF7brH.method: The analysis replaces the normalization factor with a value computed from features and dropout probability, then chooses the mean-square-optimal scalar at that fixed radius. It bounds output error under prediction-preserving replication with independent masks.
aDeomF7brH.key_idea: Fix the normalization radius using features and dropout probability, then optimally rescale only the output component affected by normalization.
aDeomF7brH.evidence: Replication bounds and an RMS-normalization rate obstruction accompany experiments on MNIST networks, a pretrained FaceNet embedding, and thirteen language models.

HhyB6932wc.one_liner: Resetting target worlds and controlling transferred artifacts tests whether Minecraft agents acquire reusable capabilities from experience.
HhyB6932wc.problem: Saved memories and successful actions do not distinguish transferable capability acquisition from carried-over resources, unequal exposure, or execution failures.
HhyB6932wc.method: MC-EvoBench represents tasks as state graphs with stage verifiers and matched source and target roles. It resets target worlds and permits only declared agent artifacts to transfer, comparing source conditions under matched step budgets.
HhyB6932wc.key_idea: Isolate experience transfer by resetting target worlds, restricting transferred artifacts, and comparing matched source conditions with graph-based stage verification.
HhyB6932wc.evidence: Minecraft evaluation uses 19 evolution chains, three paired probe families, and five seeds, finding no stable transfer from related experience.

5csjVMvT1H.one_liner: CtrlWAM pairs perturbed actions with simulated visual outcomes and warps video-action noise schedules for joint prediction.
5csjVMvT1H.problem: Adding noise independently to recorded actions and future video pairs counterfactual actions with visuals tied to the original recording.
5csjVMvT1H.method: CtrlWAM executes perturbed actions in a simulator and trains on their noised visual consequences using warped video-action noise schedules. It also supports a variable number of agent action streams.
5csjVMvT1H.key_idea: Pair perturbed actions with their simulated visual consequences and coordinate video-action denoising through warped noise schedules.
5csjVMvT1H.evidence: Driving and robotics experiments assess forecasts, video-action agreement, command following, motion fidelity, and controllability, with matched controls for off-path renders.

Ad1LFpbkZk.one_liner: MessageFlow prefills stable prompt prefixes during idle and decode periods, reusing their KV states when agents run.
Ad1LFpbkZk.problem: Agent-centric on-device execution delays prompt processing until invocation despite earlier input availability and underused GPU capacity.
Ad1LFpbkZk.method: MessageFlow identifies reusable prompt prefixes from message updates, dependencies, and prompt order. Its runtime prioritizes incremental prefills during GPU opportunities and reuses resulting KV states at agent invocation.
Ad1LFpbkZk.key_idea: Compute stable prompt prefixes before agent invocation during available GPU periods and reuse their KV states.
Ad1LFpbkZk.evidence: Implemented on LangGraph and SGLang, MessageFlow is evaluated on three representative workflows and four locally deployed LLMs.

m3PjV9TV3a.one_liner: A two-dimensional evaluation criterion combines LLM accuracy with estimated distance between benchmark inputs and training distributions.
m3PjV9TV3a.problem: Benchmark accuracy can conflate language-model capability with proximity to the model's training-data distribution.
m3PjV9TV3a.method: The paper approximates distributional distance between evaluation inputs and LLM training data and measures its correlation with accuracy. It proposes jointly evaluating accuracy and distributional distance.
m3PjV9TV3a.key_idea: Assess models using both benchmark accuracy and estimated input-to-training distributional distance.
m3PjV9TV3a.evidence: The paper empirically studies the accuracy-distance correlation and re-evaluates nine LLMs on thirteen standard benchmarks.

R4Ah5TQnHt.one_liner: DJT shares a transformer backbone between latent denoising and image reconstruction, with separate task-specific heads.
R4Ah5TQnHt.problem: Generated and encoded latent distributions differ, creating tension between reconstruction fidelity and latent generative modeling.
R4Ah5TQnHt.method: DJT jointly trains a shared backbone with denoising and reconstruction objectives and specialized heads. At inference it iteratively denoises a latent and then decodes it into an image using the same model.
R4Ah5TQnHt.key_idea: Jointly train denoising and reconstruction on a shared backbone, then reuse it sequentially for latent generation and image decoding.
R4Ah5TQnHt.evidence: ImageNet experiments evaluate DJT-XL, and representation analyses assess alignment and functional compatibility between denoising and decoding.
R4Ah5TQnHt.claimed_gains: DJT-XL achieves gFID=0.97 on ImageNet with 30% less parameters than the counterpart pipeline.

yiqZvMKK6B.one_liner: LEAP ranks short windows within recording blocks and re-encodes selected audio-video evidence in a bounded answer pass.
yiqZvMKK6B.problem: Whole-recording encoding exceeds context limits, while uniform compression loses fine acoustic and visual evidence in long audio-video question answering.
yiqZvMKK6B.method: LEAP scores candidate windows within fixed-duration blocks, pools the highest-ranked windows, and re-encodes them for answering. Separate localization and answer LoRAs train selection and reasoning, with transcript-based localization and raw audio-video answering.
yiqZvMKK6B.key_idea: Localize evidence independently within temporal blocks, then answer from the highest-ranked windows in a fixed-size context.
yiqZvMKK6B.evidence: Experiments on several AVQA benchmarks compare against Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B and report transfer to a second omni-modal model.
yiqZvMKK6B.claimed_gains: LEAP improves over Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B by 4.5–16.8% across several AVQA benchmarks.

as6scDGsKJ.one_liner: A tool-selecting proposer and faithfulness-trained actor produce model-grounded explanations across tabular, text, and vision tasks.
as6scDGsKJ.problem: Domain practitioners lack the expertise to select, interpret, and combine post-hoc explanation tools, while LLM explanations can be unfaithful.
as6scDGsKJ.method: MEA uses a Proposer to configure explanation tools and an Actor to turn their outputs into natural-language explanations. The Actor is optimized with perturbation-based faithfulness rewards and a modality-adaptive penalty.
as6scDGsKJ.key_idea: Separate explanation-tool selection from explanation generation, training the generating actor against perturbation-based faithfulness rewards and a modality-adaptive penalty.
as6scDGsKJ.evidence: Evaluation spans six datasets across tabular, text, and vision modalities, with feature-attribution, counterfactual, and spurious-feature questions and comparisons against explainers and agentic baselines.

E7UflNmgJ1.one_liner: Coupled pattern and motion states evolve through graph-wave transitions for spatio-temporal prediction.
E7UflNmgJ1.problem: Snapshot-first graph models do not explicitly represent pattern motion, although identical present fields can have different futures depending on recent change.
E7UflNmgJ1.method: WaveGSSM maintains each node's latent pattern and its temporal rate of change. A second-order graph-wave transition updates motion through graph interactions and uses that motion to advance the pattern.
E7UflNmgJ1.key_idea: Maintain coupled pattern and temporal-derivative states, updating motion through graph interactions before advancing the pattern.
E7UflNmgJ1.evidence: Evaluation covers four temporal-graph benchmarks and global weather forecasting against a backbone-matched snapshot model.
